title: Inspect bank reconciliations for independent review
description:
Objective: Determine whether the bank reconciliation control operates as designed.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Select a sample of monthly bank reconciliations, including year-end.
2. Inspect each for evidence of preparation date, independent reviewer sign-off, and follow-up of outstanding items.
3. Note reconciliations prepared late, reviewed by the preparer, or carrying aged unexplained items.

Population: Bank reconciliations for the period.

Sampling notes: Sample across months, always including the year-end reconciliation.

Expected result: Reconciliations are prepared promptly and show evidence of independent review, with aged items investigated.

Exception criteria: Reconciliations unsigned or reviewed by the preparer; long-outstanding items carried without investigation; reconciliations prepared months late.

Follow-up: Review failures are control deficiencies, not proof of misstatement. Assess the deficiency and expand substantive procedures over the bank balance and outstanding items.

title: Reperform the year-end bank reconciliation
description:
Objective: Independently verify the year-end bank reconciliation.

Technique: Reperformance

Steps: 1. Obtain the year-end bank reconciliation, the cash book and the bank statement.
2. Independently reperform the reconciliation: agree the cash book and bank statement balances, and re-list outstanding items.
3. Verify each reconciling item is valid and dated correctly.

Population: Year-end bank reconciliation and supporting records.

Sampling notes: Census of the year-end reconciliation.

Expected result: The reperformance agrees with the client's reconciliation; reconciling items are valid and correctly dated.

Exception criteria: Reperformance differs from the client's reconciliation; reconciling items unsupported or misdated.

Follow-up: Investigate differences; quantify the effect on the reported cash balance; if the reconciliation does not reconcile, treat the cash balance as uncorroborated and extend procedures.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Vouch aged outstanding items to subsequent clearance
description:
Objective: Verify that outstanding items in the bank reconciliation are genuine.

Technique: Vouching

Steps: 1. Obtain the aged outstanding items schedule at the reporting date.
2. Trace each material and aged item to the subsequent bank statement to confirm clearance.
3. For items not cleared, inspect supporting documents and obtain explanations.

Population: Outstanding items at the reporting date.

Sampling notes: Census of material and aged items; sample of routine recent items.

Expected result: Each material outstanding item clears shortly after the reporting date or is validly explained.

Exception criteria: Outstanding items that never clear; deposits in transit with no subsequent receipt; cheques outstanding for months.

Follow-up: For items that do not clear, investigate with management; consider whether the cash balance is overstated and propose adjustment; stale items may indicate the reconciliation is being used to conceal differences.

title: Obtain direct bank confirmation of balances
description:
Objective: Obtain independent confirmation of bank balances at the reporting date.

Technique: External confirmation

Steps: 1. Prepare bank confirmation requests for all accounts, controlled by the auditor throughout.
2. Send requests directly to the banks and receive responses directly.
3. Agree confirmed balances to the bank reconciliations and investigate differences.

Population: All bank accounts.

Sampling notes: Census of bank accounts, including closed accounts.

Expected result: The confirmed balance agrees with the reconciled bank balance; all accounts are captured.

Exception criteria: Confirmed balance differs from the reconciled balance; confirmation reveals accounts not in the books.

Follow-up: Investigate differences; unrecorded accounts or facilities may indicate completeness issues or undisclosed borrowings.

title: Vouch unusual payments to supporting documentation
description:
Objective: Verify that unusual payments to unfamiliar beneficiaries are genuine and properly supported.

Technique: Vouching

Steps: 1. Extract payments to new or unfamiliar beneficiaries from the payment register.
2. For a sample, vouch each payment to supporting documents: invoice or contract, approval, and evidence of goods or services received.
3. Verify the beneficiary's details against the verification records and the bank instruction.

Population: Payments to new or unfamiliar beneficiaries in the period.

Sampling notes: Risk-based sample: all large or round-sum payments to new beneficiaries; sample of smaller ones.

Expected result: Each sampled payment is supported by valid documentation consistent with the beneficiary, amount and business purpose.

Exception criteria: Payments with no supporting documents; documents inconsistent with the payment (wrong beneficiary, altered amounts); payments with no business purpose.

Follow-up: Investigate each unsupported payment with management; trace the funds where possible; quantify improper payments; evaluate fraud risk indicators without presuming fraud.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Analyse payments by beneficiary for anomalies
description:
Objective: Identify anomalous payment patterns indicative of improper beneficiaries.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Analyse payments by beneficiary: new beneficiaries, payment frequency, round sums, and amounts relative to approval thresholds.
2. Compare beneficiary names and bank details for near-duplicates.
3. Investigate anomalies against purchase history and business operations.

Population: Full payment register for the period.

Sampling notes: Full-population scan; targeted follow-up of exceptions.

Expected result: Payment patterns are consistent with the business's known suppliers and operations; anomalies are explained.

Exception criteria: Beneficiaries appearing suddenly with large payments; round-sum payments; payments just below approval thresholds; duplicate beneficiary names with different bank details.

Follow-up: Vouch anomalies to supporting documentation and beneficiary verification records; investigate with management.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Trace new beneficiaries to verification evidence
description:
Objective: Verify that new beneficiaries are subject to independent verification before payment.

Technique: Tracing

Steps: 1. Obtain the list of beneficiaries added in the period.
2. For a sample, trace each to the beneficiary verification record and supporting documents.
3. Confirm verification predates the first payment.

Population: Beneficiaries added in the period.

Sampling notes: Sample of new beneficiaries, weighted toward the largest first payments.

Expected result: Each new beneficiary paid in the period was independently verified before the first payment.

Exception criteria: New beneficiaries paid with no verification record; verification performed after the first payment.

Follow-up: For unverified beneficiaries, perform full vouching of their payments; assess the control deficiency.

title: Test payment authorisation controls
description:
Objective: Test whether payment authorisation controls operate as designed.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Select a sample of payment batches.
2. Inspect each for the required authorisations (including dual authorisation above thresholds).
3. Verify supporting documents were matched to the payment before release.

Population: Payment batches in the period.

Sampling notes: Sample across the period, including large and unusual payments.

Expected result: Payments show the required authorisations with supporting documents matched before release.

Exception criteria: Payments released without required authorisation; single authorisation where dual is required; supporting documents not matched.

Follow-up: Authorisation failures are control deficiencies, not proof payments were improper. Increase substantive vouching of payments released without proper authorisation.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Match both sides of year-end transfers
description:
Objective: Verify that inter-account transfers around year-end are recorded in the correct period on both sides.

Technique: Cut-off testing

Steps: 1. Obtain the transfer register and bank statements for all accounts for the cut-off window.
2. For each transfer, match the debit on the sending account to the credit on the receiving account, noting value dates.
3. Verify each side is recorded in the correct period and that in-transit amounts are not double-counted.

Population: All inter-account transfers in the cut-off window around the reporting date.

Sampling notes: Census of material transfers in the cut-off window.

Expected result: Each year-end transfer is recorded in the correct period on both sides; in-transit amounts are correctly presented.

Exception criteria: Transfers recorded as received before the value date; transfers recorded on one side only at year-end; in-transit amounts included in cash without disclosure of the double-count.

Follow-up: Quantify cut-off errors and propose adjustments; if transfers were used to inflate cash deliberately, reassess fraud risk and consider the implications for the audit.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Inspect transfer advices and bank statements
description:
Objective: Corroborate recorded year-end transfers to bank-issued evidence.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Obtain bank transfer advices for material transfers around the reporting date.
2. Agree amount, accounts and value dates to the transfer register and bank statements.
3. Note transfers reversed shortly after year-end and obtain explanations.

Population: Material year-end transfers.

Sampling notes: Census of material transfers in the cut-off window.

Expected result: Transfer advices support the recorded transfers, with value dates consistent with the period of recording.

Exception criteria: Advices missing for recorded transfers; value dates inconsistent with recording; transfers reversed shortly after year-end without explanation.

Follow-up: Investigate missing or inconsistent advices; post year-end reversals may indicate window dressing and require reassessment of the cash position.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Reperform the in-transit reconciliation
description:
Objective: Verify the completeness and accuracy of the year-end in-transit position.

Technique: Reperformance

Steps: 1. Reperform the in-transit schedule from the transfer register and bank statements.
2. Verify each in-transit item appears once: excluded from the sending account and either in transit or received, not both.
3. Agree the resulting cash position to the reported balance.

Population: In-transit items at the reporting date.

Sampling notes: Census of in-transit items at year-end.

Expected result: The in-transit schedule reconciles: amounts in transit at year-end are identified once and correctly presented.

Exception criteria: In-transit schedule that does not reconcile; in-transit amounts included in the cash balance twice.

Follow-up: Propose adjustments for double-counted or omitted amounts; if material, evaluate the effect on the audit opinion.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Count cash on hand
description:
Objective: Obtain direct evidence of the existence of cash on hand.

Technique: Physical verification

Steps: 1. Arrive unannounced and take control of all cash at each location simultaneously.
2. Count cash by denomination and record independently; include undeposited receipts.
3. Have the count acknowledged by the custodian and retain a copy of the count record.

Population: Cash on hand at the count date (tills, petty cash, undeposited receipts).

Sampling notes: Surprise count; all cash locations counted simultaneously where practicable.

Expected result: Cash counted agrees with the cash records; any difference is explained and supported.

Exception criteria: Counted cash less than the recorded balance; IOUs or personal items held as cash; cashier unable to explain differences.

Follow-up: Investigate shortages with the cashier and management; quantify the loss; assess whether the pattern indicates misappropriation - without presuming it - and consider the implications for the control environment.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Reconcile the count to cash records and investigate differences
description:
Objective: Verify that counted cash reconciles to the records and differences are properly dealt with.

Technique: Reperformance

Steps: 1. Reconcile the counted total to the petty cash records and cash book.
2. Inspect IOUs or other non-cash items found; verify they are not included in the cash balance.
3. Investigate and document the resolution of each difference.

Population: Cash count results and cash records at the count date.

Sampling notes: Not applicable - reconciliation of the count.

Expected result: The count reconciles to the cash records; differences are investigated, approved and correctly treated (IOUs are not cash).

Exception criteria: Unreconciled differences; IOUs included in the cash balance; shortages written off without approval.

Follow-up: Quantify shortages; determine whether they indicate error or misappropriation; propose adjustment where the recorded balance is overstated.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Observe the entity's cash count procedures
description:
Objective: Determine whether the entity's cash count controls operate as designed.

Technique: Observation

Steps: 1. Observe an entity cash count where one is scheduled, noting independence and surprise.
2. Inspect count sheets and reconciliations for other counts in the period.
3. Note whether differences were investigated and approved.

Population: Cash counts performed in the period.

Sampling notes: Observe at least one count; inspect records of others.

Expected result: Counts are performed by an independent person, unannounced, with differences investigated.

Exception criteria: Counts performed by the cashier alone; announced counts; differences not followed up.

Follow-up: Weaknesses in count discipline are control deficiencies. Increase the extent of the auditor's own physical verification.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Journal entry testing for management override
description:
Objective: Detect manual journal entries used to manipulate reported results, including management override of controls.

Technique: Reperformance

Steps: 1. Obtain a complete extract of manual journals directly from the system and reconcile the population to the general ledger movements.
2. Stratify the population using risk flags: entries posted at or after period-end, outside normal hours, by senior management, in round amounts, to seldom-used or sensitive accounts, and entries with blank or vague descriptions.
3. For selected entries, inspect supporting documentation, verify independent approval, and evaluate the business rationale.
4. Trace a sample of entries through to the financial statements to confirm correct recording.

Population: All manual journal entries posted in the period (complete system extract, reconciled to the general ledger).

Sampling notes: Stratified selection, not random sampling: 100% of entries matching high-risk flags (period-end, outside hours, senior management, round amounts, seldom-used accounts, post-closing), plus a sample of the remainder.

Expected result: Tested journals are authorised, supported by valid business rationale, and correctly recorded; the stratification identifies no unexplained concentration of high-risk entries.

Exception criteria: Material unsupported or unauthorised journals; journals that lack any business rationale; a pattern of period-end entries that consistently improve reported results.

Follow-up: Investigate each exception with management and corroborate explanations independently. If explanations are inadequate, extend testing to similar entries, quantify the potential misstatement, and reassess fraud risk - including whether those charged with governance need to be informed. Do NOT automatically conclude that fraud has occurred; consider escalation proportionate to the evidence.

title: Unpredictable audit procedures
description:
Objective: Reduce the risk that management anticipates audit procedures and conceals fraud in untested areas.

Technique: Reperformance

Steps: 1. Vary the timing of procedures (e.g. interim vs year-end) compared with the prior year.
2. Select different locations, branches or business units from those covered previously.
3. Test account balances and transaction streams that were below the testing threshold last year.
4. Perform at least one procedure without forewarning the entity (e.g. a surprise count or an unannounced confirmation date).

Population: Varies by year: locations, balances, transaction streams and timing.

Sampling notes: Deliberately non-statistical: choose what was NOT covered last year and what management would least expect.

Expected result: The varied procedures are performed as planned and their results are consistent with the rest of the audit evidence.

Exception criteria: Unpredictable procedures repeatedly uncover issues in areas previously tested clean, suggesting prior procedures were anticipated and circumvented.

Follow-up: Where unpredicted selections reveal issues, investigate fully and consider whether the pattern suggests deliberate concealment - reassess fraud risk and extend procedures accordingly, without presuming fraud.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Retrospective review of prior-year significant estimates
description:
Objective: Identify indicators of systematic management bias in significant accounting estimates.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. List the significant estimates made in the prior period and the key assumptions behind each.
2. Compare each estimate with the actual outcome now known, quantifying the difference and its direction.
3. Assess whether differences cluster in the direction favourable to reported results.
4. Evaluate whether the pattern indicates bias affecting current-period estimates and challenge those assumptions accordingly.

Population: All significant accounting estimates from the prior period where outcomes are now known.

Sampling notes: Census of significant estimates; bias is assessed from the pattern across estimates, not from any single one.

Expected result: Prior estimates proved reasonable in light of actual outcomes, with no systematic directional pattern.

Exception criteria: Estimates consistently resolved in the direction favourable to reported results, or assumptions repeatedly at the optimistic end of the range.

Follow-up: A pattern of optimistic outcomes is a bias indicator, not proof of fraud: discuss with management, challenge current-year assumptions with heightened scepticism, consider involving those charged with governance, and evaluate the aggregate effect on the financial statements.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Business-rationale testing of significant unusual transactions
description:
Objective: Determine whether significant unusual transactions (especially with related parties) have genuine business substance or were structured to misstate the financial statements.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Identify significant transactions outside the normal course of business, near period-end, or with related parties.
2. Obtain and inspect the underlying contracts, approvals and correspondence.
3. Evaluate whether the terms, timing and economics make commercial sense.
4. Where applicable, confirm key terms directly with the counterparty and trace the cash flows.

Population: All transactions identified as significant and unusual (size, nature, timing, counterparty).

Sampling notes: Census of significant unusual transactions; professional judgment defines the threshold.

Expected result: Each significant unusual transaction has a clear, documented business rationale consistent with the entity's strategy.

Exception criteria: Transactions with no discernible business purpose, circular cash flows, or counterparties that cannot be verified as independent.

Follow-up: Where rationale is absent or unconvincing, extend procedures: confirm terms with counterparties, inspect cash flows, and evaluate whether the transaction was designed to misstate the financial statements. Escalate to those charged with governance if management cannot explain the transaction. Do not presume fraud from an unusual transaction alone.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Surprise cash and inventory verification
description:
Objective: Obtain direct evidence of cash and inventory existence without giving the entity an opportunity to conceal shortages.

Technique: Physical verification

Steps: 1. Without prior notice, attend selected locations and take control of cash and inventory areas.
2. Count cash by denomination and test-count inventory in both directions, recording results independently.
3. Reconcile to the books on the spot and investigate differences immediately with custodians.

Population: Cash on hand and physical inventory at selected locations.

Sampling notes: Unannounced timing; locations weighted toward weak oversight and high-value holdings.

Expected result: Physical quantities agree with records (subject to investigated differences); cash counted agrees with the book balance.

Exception criteria: Unexplained shortages, cash or inventory that cannot be located, or records that do not match physical quantities.

Follow-up: Investigate all differences immediately while on site; if shortages are unexplained, extend counts, review access and custody records, and reassess fraud risk. Treat indicators as requiring investigation, not as conclusions.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Related-party completeness search
description:
Objective: Detect related-party relationships and transactions that management has not disclosed.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Inspect shareholder registers, directorship records and organisational charts for the full period.
2. Review board minutes for discussion of related parties and undisclosed arrangements.
3. Scan material contracts and transactions for related-party indicators (shared addresses, officers, non-arm's-length terms).
4. Cross-check findings against management's related-party listing and investigate omissions.

Population: Shareholder and directorship registers, board minutes, organisational charts, and material transaction documentation.

Sampling notes: Targeted search, not sampling: follow names, addresses and shared officers across sources.

Expected result: The related-party population is complete; all identified relationships and material transactions are disclosed.

Exception criteria: Undisclosed related parties identified; material transactions with parties whose relationship was concealed.

Follow-up: For each newly identified party, identify all transactions and balances, evaluate disclosure, and consider why the party was undisclosed - concealment may indicate fraud risk elsewhere. Inform those charged with governance of the findings.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Inspect manual journals and vouch to supporting documentation
description:
Objective: Determine whether manual journals represent genuine, supportable adjustments.

Technique: Vouching

Steps: 1. Obtain the complete listing of manual journal entries for the period and confirm its completeness to the general ledger.
2. Select journals for testing, weighting selection toward period-end entries, large or round amounts, and entries posted by senior management.
3. For each selected journal, inspect the supporting documentation and evaluate whether it justifies the amount, the accounts debited and credited, and the period recorded.
4. Verify that each material journal was approved by someone independent of the preparer.
5. Document journals lacking adequate support as exceptions for follow-up.

Population: All manual journal entries posted in the period.

Sampling notes: Stratified selection weighted toward period-end and post-closing journals, large or round amounts, and journals posted by senior staff; include a random element.

Expected result: Each tested journal is supported by documentation that justifies the amount, the accounts used and the period, and was approved independently of the preparer.

Exception criteria: Journals with no support, inadequate support, or support that does not justify the amount or accounts used; self-approved or unapproved material journals.

Follow-up: Investigate each unsupported journal: obtain the business rationale, quantify the effect, and consider whether the pattern (timing, preparer, accounts) indicates a systematic issue. A cluster of unsupported period-end journals is a suspected fraud indicator - investigate thoroughly, document the basis for conclusions, and never dismiss it without evidence. Do not conclude fraud from the absence of support alone.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Test independent approval of manual journals
description:
Objective: Test whether the independent-approval control over manual journals operated.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Select a sample of manual journals above the approval threshold.
2. Inspect the approval record for each: identity of approver, independence from the preparer, and timing relative to posting.
3. Test for journals that bypassed approval by comparing the journal population with approval records.
4. Note self-approvals and post-dated bulk approvals as control exceptions.

Population: Manual journals above the approval threshold in the period.

Sampling notes: Sample across the period with emphasis on period-end; include journals just above and below the threshold.

Expected result: Material manual journals are approved by an independent person before, or promptly after, posting.

Exception criteria: Material journals posted without independent approval; preparers approving their own journals; approvals obtained long after posting as a formality.

Follow-up: Treat approval failures as control exceptions; extend substantive testing of journals where the approval control did not operate; report the deficiency.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Scan the manual journal population for unusual entries
description:
Objective: Identify unusual manual journals that warrant individual investigation.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Define unusual-entry criteria: postings outside normal hours, round amounts, vague descriptions, entries by senior management, entries to seldom-used or sensitive accounts, and post-closing adjustments.
2. Scan the full manual journal population against these criteria.
3. For each flagged entry, obtain an explanation and corroborating evidence.
4. Summarise flagged entries, explanations obtained, and items remaining unexplained.

Population: The full manual journal population (computer-assisted scan).

Sampling notes: Full-population scan; investigation thresholds set with regard to materiality and the fraud risk assessment.

Expected result: Unusual entries are identified, investigated, and either satisfactorily explained with corroborating evidence or reported as exceptions.

Exception criteria: Entries exhibiting override indicators for which no satisfactory explanation and corroboration is obtained.

Follow-up: Investigate each unexplained unusual entry with the preparer and approver; corroborate explanations; if explanations are unsatisfactory, extend testing to related accounts and consider the fraud risk implications - without presuming fraud.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Perform targeted testing of journal entries for management override indicators
description:
Objective: Respond to the override risk with targeted testing of journal entries most susceptible to manipulation.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Extract journal entries exhibiting override indicators: entries made by senior management, outside normal hours, at period-end, in round amounts, to seldom-used accounts, or with vague descriptions.
2. For each selected entry, inspect the entry, its support and its approval, and evaluate the business rationale.
3. Inquire of the preparer and approver about the purpose of entries that lack an obvious rationale, and corroborate responses.
4. Evaluate the pattern of findings taken together for signs of systematic override.

Population: Journal entries (including non-standard and consolidation entries) exhibiting override indicators.

Sampling notes: Targeted selection on indicators, not statistical sampling; the population is defined by the risk, not by size.

Expected result: Each flagged entry is explained by a valid business reason supported by corroborating evidence; no pattern of inappropriate override is identified.

Exception criteria: Flagged entries with unsatisfactory explanations or corroboration; a pattern of entries directed by management outside the normal process.

Follow-up: Where explanations are unsatisfactory, extend procedures to the affected accounts, inquire of those charged with governance, and evaluate whether the matter represents a suspected fraud indicator requiring further response. Document every conclusion; do not dismiss indicators without evidence.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Inquire of those charged with governance about override and fraud
description:
Objective: Obtain the perspective of those charged with governance on override and fraud risks.

Technique: Inquiry

Steps: 1. Inquire of those charged with governance about their awareness of any actual, suspected or alleged fraud, and about their views on the risk of management override.
2. Inquire how those charged with governance exercise oversight of management's processes for identifying and responding to fraud risks.
3. Inquire of management about the same matters and compare responses.
4. Document the inquiries and follow up inconsistencies or matters raised.

Population: Those charged with governance and, separately, management.

Sampling notes: Not a sampling procedure; inquire of the appropriate individuals, including at least one person independent of management where such a person exists.

Expected result: Inquiries are documented, responses are consistent with other audit evidence, and any matters raised are followed up.

Exception criteria: Responses that are evasive, inconsistent with other audit evidence, or that reveal actual override or fraud.

Follow-up: Corroborate responses against other evidence; follow up any matter raised; if responses indicate actual override or fraud, respond accordingly under the applicable standards - escalating, extending procedures and considering implications for the audit.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Evaluate significant accounting estimates for indicators of management bias
description:
Objective: Detect whether significant accounting estimates show signs of management bias.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. For each significant estimate, compare management's assumptions with historical outcomes, market data and the auditor's independent expectations.
2. Perform sensitivity analysis to show how the estimate moves with plausible changes in assumptions.
3. Look back at prior-period estimates against actual outcomes for a pattern of optimism or pessimism.
4. Step back and evaluate whether the estimates, taken together, lean consistently in one direction.

Population: All significant accounting estimates in the period.

Sampling notes: Census of significant estimates; professional judgment determines significance.

Expected result: Significant estimates are neutral: assumptions are supportable, within a reasonable range, and any bias identified is quantified and evaluated.

Exception criteria: A pattern of assumptions consistently favouring management's reported position; estimates at the extreme optimistic end of a reasonable range without justification.

Follow-up: Quantify the effect of neutral assumptions and evaluate whether bias, individually or in aggregate, indicates a risk of material misstatement due to fraud. A one-sided pattern is a suspected fraud indicator: extend procedures, challenge further, and document the conclusion without presuming intent.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Inspect the related-party register and declarations of interest
description:
Objective: Establish the population of related parties the entity claims to have identified.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Obtain the related-party register and inspect it for completeness across the categories of related party.
2. Inspect declarations of interest from directors and key management for currency and coverage.
3. Compare the register with the prior period and investigate additions and removals.
4. Note gaps, outdated entries and missing declarations as exceptions.

Population: The related-party register and declarations of interest.

Sampling notes: Inspect the register in full; it is a population, not a sample.

Expected result: A current, complete register of related parties exists, supported by recent declarations of interest.

Exception criteria: No register maintained; register materially incomplete when compared with independent sources; declarations not obtained or outdated.

Follow-up: Where the register is incomplete, the auditor must build the related-party population independently (see the search procedure) and treat the gap as a control deficiency.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Search for undisclosed related-party relationships and transactions
description:
Objective: Independently identify related-party relationships the entity's process may have missed.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Inspect shareholder registers, corporate registry filings and organisational charts for relationships not in the register.
2. Review board minutes and significant contracts for transactions with unfamiliar counterparties or on unusual terms.
3. Scan significant and unusual transactions for indicators of related-party involvement (shared addresses, common directors or advisers, non-arm's-length terms).
4. For each indication, investigate and establish whether a related-party relationship exists.

Population: Shareholder and corporate records, board minutes, significant contracts, and unusual transactions.

Sampling notes: Targeted search; focus on unfamiliar counterparties, non-standard terms, and transactions lacking commercial logic.

Expected result: The auditor's independent search either confirms the register's completeness or identifies omissions for follow-up and disclosure.

Exception criteria: Relationships or transactions identified that were not in the entity's register or disclosures.

Follow-up: Investigate each newly identified relationship: establish the transactions with it, evaluate measurement and disclosure, and quantify omissions. Consider why the process missed it.

title: Inspect the terms and business rationale of related-party transactions
description:
Objective: Evaluate whether identified related-party transactions are genuine, appropriately measured and adequately disclosed.

Technique: Vouching

Steps: 1. Obtain the population of identified related-party transactions.
2. For each selected transaction, inspect the underlying contract or agreement and evaluate its commercial substance and business rationale.
3. Evaluate whether the terms are consistent with arm's-length terms or, where not, whether measurement reflects the actual terms.
4. Verify that the transaction is completely and understandably disclosed.

Population: All identified related-party transactions in the period.

Sampling notes: Census of material transactions; sample smaller recurring ones.

Expected result: Each tested related-party transaction has commercial substance, is measured appropriately, and its terms and rationale are documented.

Exception criteria: Transactions without commercial substance, on terms significantly off-market without justification, or lacking business rationale.

Follow-up: Challenge unsupported assertions of arm's-length terms; quantify measurement effects; evaluate disclosure; where substance is doubtful, consider the fraud risk implications without presuming fraud.

title: Inspect and challenge the assumptions underlying significant provisions
description:
Objective: Test whether the assumptions behind significant provisions are supportable.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Obtain the provision calculation schedules and identify the key assumptions driving each significant provision.
2. Inspect the supporting evidence for each assumption: legal correspondence, historical claims data, expert reports, contracts.
3. Challenge the assumptions: are they consistent with each other, with other audit evidence, and with conditions at the reporting date?
4. Inquire of management about how the assumptions were developed and corroborate the responses.

Population: Significant provisions at the reporting date.

Sampling notes: Census of significant provisions; professional judgment determines significance.

Expected result: Each key assumption is documented, consistent with available evidence (including legal advice where relevant), and within a reasonable range.

Exception criteria: Assumptions that are undocumented, contradicted by available evidence, or at an unjustified extreme of a reasonable range.

Follow-up: Develop the auditor's independent expectation and quantify the difference; propose adjustments for material differences; where assumptions cannot be supported, treat the estimate as a significant risk and extend procedures. Distinguish honest estimation uncertainty from bias: challenge the evidence, not the person.

title: Recalculate provisions and perform sensitivity analysis
description:
Objective: Verify the arithmetic of provisions and understand their sensitivity to assumptions.

Technique: Recalculation

Steps: 1. Independently recalculate each significant provision from its stated method and inputs.
2. Perform sensitivity analysis on key assumptions to establish the range of reasonable outcomes.
3. Compare the recognised amount with the auditor's independent range and with subsequent-event evidence where available.
4. Evaluate whether estimation uncertainty is adequately disclosed.

Population: Significant provision calculations.

Sampling notes: Census of significant provisions.

Expected result: Provisions are mathematically accurate and the auditor understands the sensitivity of each significant provision to its key assumptions.

Exception criteria: Recalculation differences; provisions highly sensitive to small, plausible assumption changes such that the range of reasonable outcomes includes material misstatement.

Follow-up: Where sensitivity shows a wide range of reasonable outcomes, evaluate whether the recognised amount is the best estimate within the range and whether estimation uncertainty is adequately disclosed.

title: Search for unrecorded provisions
description:
Objective: Detect obligations requiring provision or disclosure that management has not recognised.

Technique: Inquiry

Steps: 1. Review legal correspondence and board minutes for claims, disputes and regulatory matters.
2. Inquire of management and, where appropriate, legal counsel about unasserted claims and exposures.
3. Inspect contracts for onerous terms, guarantees and decommissioning obligations.
4. For each matter identified, evaluate whether a provision or disclosure is required and whether it has been made.

Population: Legal correspondence, board minutes, contracts, and correspondence about claims and disputes.

Sampling notes: Targeted search; focus on new litigation, regulatory matters, warranties and onerous contracts.

Expected result: No material unrecorded provisions are identified; where identified, they are quantified and recognised or disclosed as appropriate.

Exception criteria: Obligating events or exposures identified that have no corresponding provision or disclosure.

Follow-up: Quantify the omitted provision, propose adjustment, and investigate why the process missed it - a systematic gap is a control deficiency.

title: Complete an independent disclosure checklist
description:
Objective: Independently verify the completeness of financial statement disclosures.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Complete an independent disclosure checklist based on the applicable framework, marking each requirement as applicable or not applicable with a cross-reference.
2. Compare the checklist with the draft financial statements and identify missing or outdated disclosures.
3. Pay particular attention to new standards, new transaction types, and changed circumstances in the period.
4. Discuss each gap with management and evaluate its materiality.

Population: The disclosure requirements of the applicable financial reporting framework as at the reporting date.

Sampling notes: Not a sampling procedure; the checklist covers the full framework, tailored for applicability.

Expected result: The checklist identifies all disclosures required by the applicable framework, and each is present in the financial statements or its omission is justified.

Exception criteria: Required disclosures missing, outdated, or not updated for new transactions or standards.

Follow-up: List each missing or inadequate disclosure, discuss with management, and evaluate whether the omission is material to the financial statements taken as a whole.

title: Trace disclosure amounts to underlying records
description:
Objective: Verify the accuracy of disclosed amounts and the consistency of narrative disclosures.

Technique: Tracing

Steps: 1. Select material disclosures and trace the amounts to the underlying accounting records and supporting schedules.
2. Read narrative disclosures critically and compare them with audit evidence obtained elsewhere.
3. Verify that accounting policies disclosed are those actually applied.
4. Check internal consistency between the notes and the primary statements.

Population: Material disclosures in the notes to the financial statements.

Sampling notes: Focus on material and judgmental disclosures; census of new disclosures in the period.

Expected result: Disclosed amounts agree to the underlying accounting records and narrative disclosures are consistent with audit evidence.

Exception criteria: Disclosure amounts that do not agree to the underlying records; narrative disclosures contradicted by audit evidence.

Follow-up: Investigate and resolve each disagreement; propose corrections; evaluate whether disagreements indicate wider disclosure-control weaknesses.

title: Review new and unusual transactions for disclosure implications
description:
Objective: Ensure novel transactions have been considered for disclosure.

Technique: Inquiry

Steps: 1. Identify new, unusual or complex transactions from other audit work (journals, board minutes, contracts).
2. Inquire of management what disclosure consideration was given to each.
3. Evaluate independently whether disclosure is required and whether the proposed disclosure is adequate.
4. Document the assessment for each transaction.

Population: New, unusual or complex transactions in the period.

Sampling notes: Judgmental selection based on the auditor's knowledge of the period's activity.

Expected result: All new, unusual or complex transactions in the period have been assessed for disclosure implications and the assessment is documented.

Exception criteria: New or unusual transactions with disclosure implications that were not considered.

Follow-up: Where implications were missed, draft the required disclosure considerations and discuss with management; treat a pattern of misses as a control deficiency.

title: Inspect site leases for restoration obligations
description:
Objective: Establish the population of dismantling obligations.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Obtain the site register and select a sample of tower and rooftop sites.
2. Inspect the underlying lease or land agreements for dismantling and site-restoration clauses.
3. Agree the restoration-clause flag in the register to the contract terms.

Population: Network site leases.

Sampling notes: Stratify by site type and geography; include new sites in the year.

Expected result: Sites with restoration obligations are completely and accurately flagged in the register.

Exception criteria: Restoration clauses found in contracts but missing from the register; register sites with no supporting agreement.

Follow-up: Quantify the unrecognised obligation; extend the sample; consider whether the omission indicates a systematic completeness failure - do not presume intent.

title: Recalculate the decommissioning provision and challenge assumptions
description:
Objective: Test the measurement of the recognised provision.

Technique: Recalculation

Steps: 1. Obtain the provision model and independently recalculate it.
2. Challenge key assumptions: per-site dismantling cost, expected timing, discount rate and inflation.
3. Verify the unwinding of discount is recognised and the capitalised asset cost is depreciated.

Population: Decommissioning provision by site cohort.

Sampling notes: Reperform the full model; sensitivity-test key assumptions.

Expected result: The provision recalculates; assumptions are supportable and consistent with contracts and market data.

Exception criteria: Material recalculation differences; unsupported cost or discount assumptions; unwinding omitted.

Follow-up: Propose adjustments for unsupported measurement; perform sensitivity analysis to assess estimation uncertainty for disclosure.

title: Reperform allocation of consideration on a sample of bundled contracts
description:
Objective: Test accuracy of the allocation and timing of recognition.

Technique: Reperformance

Steps: 1. Select a sample of new bundled contracts across tariff plans.
2. Obtain the contract terms and the stand-alone selling prices used.
3. Independently reperform the allocation and compare with the amounts recognised.

Population: New bundled contracts in the period.

Sampling notes: Stratify by tariff plan, including newly launched plans.

Expected result: Allocation agrees with the reperformance; recognition timing follows delivery of each component.

Exception criteria: Material allocation differences; revenue recognised before service delivery.

Follow-up: Extend testing to the affected tariff plan; quantify the timing misstatement; assess whether the configuration error is systematic.

title: Inspect tariff plan approvals and allocation configuration
description:
Objective: Verify allocation keys were properly authorised.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Obtain approval documentation for a sample of tariff plans launched in the period.
2. Verify the stand-alone selling prices are supported (e.g. observable prices) and approved.
3. Trace the approved configuration into the billing system.

Population: Tariff plans launched in the period.

Sampling notes: Focus on plans with the highest subscriber uptake.

Expected result: Approvals exist, are independent, and match the system configuration.

Exception criteria: Launched plans without approval; configuration differing from approval.

Follow-up: Treat unapproved configurations as a control deficiency; expand substantive allocation testing for those plans.

title: Reperform rating on a sample of usage records
description:
Objective: Test accuracy of automated rating independently of the system.

Technique: Reperformance

Steps: 1. Extract a sample of rated usage records (CDRs) across tariff types.
2. Independently apply the published tariff to compute the expected charge.
3. Compare with the billed amount and investigate differences.

Population: Rated usage records in the period.

Sampling notes: Stratify by tariff and service type; include records from just after tariff changes.

Expected result: Reperformed charges agree with billed amounts.

Exception criteria: Systematic differences for a tariff or service type; unexplained rejected records.

Follow-up: Quantify the affected population; determine whether the error is systematic and requires a provision or restatement of billed revenue.

title: Test follow-up of rating exceptions and rejections
description:
Objective: Verify rejected usage is completely resolved.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Obtain rating exception/rejection logs for the period.
2. Select a sample of exceptions and inspect evidence of investigation and resolution.
3. Trace reprocessed records into billing.

Population: Rating exceptions and rejections.

Sampling notes: Focus on high-value and recurring exception types.

Expected result: Exceptions are investigated timely; valid usage is reprocessed into billing.

Exception criteria: Unresolved or written-off exceptions without justification; material rejected volumes.

Follow-up: Estimate unrecorded revenue from unresolved rejections; report the control gap.

title: Reperform overhead absorption and challenge the rate
description:
Objective: Test the accuracy of overhead absorbed into WIP.

Technique: Recalculation

Steps: 1. Obtain the overhead absorption model and independently recalculate it.
2. Verify the rate to approved budgets and actual overhead pools.
3. Assess whether the normal-capacity assumption is reasonable against actual utilisation.

Population: Overhead absorbed in the period.

Sampling notes: Reperform the full model; sensitivity-test the capacity assumption.

Expected result: Absorption recalculates; the rate and capacity basis are supportable.

Exception criteria: Material recalculation differences; rates based on superseded budgets; abnormal idle costs absorbed.

Follow-up: Quantify the WIP misstatement; propose adjustment; consider whether other estimates share the same weak budgeting inputs.

title: Test WIP by physical observation and stage-of-completion
description:
Objective: Corroborate the existence and completion stage of WIP.

Technique: Physical verification

Steps: 1. Attend the physical count and observe WIP quantities and production stages.
2. For sampled WIP jobs, inspect job cards and agree stage-of-completion to costs incurred.
3. Challenge whether stalled or obsolete jobs remain in WIP.

Population: WIP at the reporting date.

Sampling notes: Focus on high-value jobs and jobs open for unusually long periods.

Expected result: WIP exists, stages agree with cost records, and stalled jobs are provided for.

Exception criteria: WIP jobs that cannot be located; stages inconsistent with costs; obsolete jobs carried at full cost.

Follow-up: Propose write-downs for obsolete WIP; extend testing if stage assessments appear optimistic.

title: Analyse variances and test standard-to-actual alignment
description:
Objective: Determine whether standards remain appropriate and variances are understood.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Obtain variance reports for the period and identify material variances.
2. For material variances, inspect investigation documentation or perform the investigation.
3. Compare standards to recent actual costs for major inputs.

Population: Cost variances in the period.

Sampling notes: Census of material variances; trend analysis over the year.

Expected result: Material variances are explained by valid causes and standards approximate actual costs.

Exception criteria: Material unexplained variances; standards materially divorced from actual costs.

Follow-up: Quantify the inventory impact of stale standards; propose adjustment; recommend standards revision.

title: Inspect disposition of variances
description:
Objective: Verify variances are correctly allocated between inventory and cost of sales.

Technique: Tracing

Steps: 1. Trace material variances from the variance report to the ledger.
2. Verify the allocation between closing inventory and cost of sales is appropriate.
3. Check that immaterial variances are treated consistently.

Population: Material variance journals.

Sampling notes: Census of material items.

Expected result: Variances are completely recorded and appropriately allocated.

Exception criteria: Variances posted entirely to cost of sales to avoid inventory adjustment; unrecorded variances.

Follow-up: Recompute the correct allocation; propose adjustments where inventory is misstated.

title: Test the warranty provision against claim experience
description:
Objective: Assess whether the provision reflects actual and expected claims.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Obtain the provision model and claims data by product cohort.
2. Compare historical provisions with actual claims paid (back-testing).
3. Challenge assumptions for new products with no history.

Population: Warranty provision and claims.

Sampling notes: Cohort-level analysis; focus on new or high-claim products.

Expected result: Provisions track actual claim experience; new-product assumptions are cautious and supported.

Exception criteria: Systematic under-provisioning revealed by back-testing; new products with no provision.

Follow-up: Propose adjustment based on claim experience; evaluate disclosure of the estimation uncertainty.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Inspect warranty terms and identify unprovided obligations
description:
Objective: Establish the complete population of warranty obligations.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Inspect standard warranty terms and any extended warranties sold or given.
2. Verify all products sold with warranty cover are in the provision population.
3. Check cut-off: sales before year-end are included.

Population: Products sold with warranty.

Sampling notes: Include new product lines launched in the year.

Expected result: All warranty-bearing sales are captured in the provision.

Exception criteria: Product lines omitted; extended warranties not provided for.

Follow-up: Quantify the omitted obligation; extend procedures to the affected lines.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Reconcile till records to bankings and investigate differences
description:
Objective: Test completeness of recorded sales and existence of cash.

Technique: Recalculation

Steps: 1. Select a sample of trading days and outlets.
2. Agree till Z-readings to daily sales records and to bankings.
3. Investigate differences and inspect supporting void/refund documentation.

Population: Daily till records and bankings.

Sampling notes: Surprise selection; include high-cash outlets.

Expected result: Till records agree to bankings; differences are explained and supported.

Exception criteria: Unexplained shortfalls; unsupported voids/refunds; pattern of differences at an outlet.

Follow-up: Extend testing at affected outlets; consider unannounced cash counts; evaluate fraud indicators without presuming fraud.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Perform analytical procedures on sales, voids and refunds
description:
Objective: Identify unusual patterns indicative of skimming or error.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Compare sales, void rates, refund rates and discounts by outlet and period.
2. Investigate outlets or periods that are outliers.
3. Correlate with inventory shrinkage where available.

Population: Outlet-level sales data.

Sampling notes: Full-population analytics; threshold-based investigation.

Expected result: Outlet metrics are consistent; outliers have valid explanations.

Exception criteria: Outlets with abnormal void/refund rates or sales dips without cause.

Follow-up: Target substantive testing at outlier outlets; discuss findings with management.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Vouch rebate income to supplier agreements and confirm with suppliers
description:
Objective: Test that recognised rebates are agreed and earned.

Technique: Vouching

Steps: 1. Select material rebate streams and inspect the underlying supplier agreements.
2. Recompute the rebate earned from purchase volumes and agreed tiers.
3. Confirm material year-end accruals directly with suppliers.

Population: Rebate income and receivables.

Sampling notes: Cover the largest suppliers and all material accruals.

Expected result: Rebates agree to signed terms and earned volumes; supplier confirmations agree.

Exception criteria: Unsigned or disputed terms; confirmations disagreeing; income recognised above earned tiers.

Follow-up: Propose adjustments for unconfirmed or unearned rebates; extend confirmation where disputes exist.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Test cut-off of rebate accruals
description:
Objective: Verify rebates are recognised in the correct period.

Technique: Cut-off testing

Steps: 1. Obtain the year-end rebate accrual and the volume data behind it.
2. Verify qualifying volumes were achieved before the reporting date.
3. Check post-year-end supplier statements for contradictory terms.

Population: Year-end rebate accruals.

Sampling notes: Census of material accruals.

Expected result: Accruals reflect volumes achieved in the period on agreed terms.

Exception criteria: Accruals based on forecast volumes; terms agreed after year-end.

Follow-up: Reverse or adjust premature accruals; assess whether the pattern indicates systematic optimism.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Reconcile gift card and loyalty liabilities and test breakage
description:
Objective: Test completeness of deferred revenue and reasonableness of breakage.

Technique: Recalculation

Steps: 1. Reconcile the loyalty/POS liability reports to the general ledger.
2. Test a sample of redemptions from liability to revenue.
3. Challenge the breakage rate against historical redemption patterns.

Population: Gift card and loyalty liabilities.

Sampling notes: Full reconciliation; sample redemptions across schemes.

Expected result: Liabilities reconcile; breakage is consistent with redemption history.

Exception criteria: Unreconciled differences; breakage rates without historical support; releases without redemption.

Follow-up: Propose adjustments for unsupported breakage; extend testing where liabilities do not reconcile.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Test cut-off of redemptions around the reporting date
description:
Objective: Verify releases from deferred revenue occur on actual redemption.

Technique: Cut-off testing

Steps: 1. Select redemptions around year-end and trace to POS/loyalty system evidence.
2. Verify releases before year-end relate to genuine redemptions.
3. Inspect expiry policies and their consistent application.

Population: Redemptions near the reporting date.

Sampling notes: Focus on the last and first days of the period.

Expected result: Releases match genuine redemptions in the correct period.

Exception criteria: Bulk releases without redemption evidence; inconsistent expiry application.

Follow-up: Reverse unsupported releases; investigate the business rationale for bulk adjustments.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Challenge staging, parameters and overlays in the ECL model
description:
Objective: Test the reasonableness of the impairment estimate.

Technique: Reperformance

Steps: 1. Understand the model, staging criteria and forward-looking scenarios.
2. Test a sample of staging decisions, including overrides, against the criteria.
3. Challenge PD/LGD parameters and the rationale for management overlays; perform sensitivity analysis.

Population: Loan portfolio and ECL model.

Sampling notes: Risk-based: borderline staging cases, large exposures, overlays.

Expected result: Staging follows the criteria; parameters are supportable; overlays are justified and directionally consistent.

Exception criteria: Systematic staging overrides deferring stage 2; stale parameters; overlays suppressing the charge without basis.

Follow-up: Develop an independent range; propose adjustments where the booked ECL falls outside it; evaluate disclosure adequacy.

title: Test credit risk disclosures
description:
Objective: Verify completeness and accuracy of credit risk disclosures.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Agree disclosed exposures, staging movements and coverage ratios to the model outputs.
2. Verify sensitivity disclosures reflect the model's actual sensitivities.
3. Check that significant judgments are described.

Population: Credit risk disclosures.

Sampling notes: Not applicable - full disclosure set.

Expected result: Disclosures agree to underlying records and describe the key judgments.

Exception criteria: Disclosed figures that do not agree; missing sensitivity or staging disclosures.

Follow-up: Require corrected or expanded disclosure; consider the implication for the audit report if refused.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Test suspension of interest on non-performing loans
description:
Objective: Verify interest is not accrued where collection is doubtful.

Technique: Reperformance

Steps: 1. Obtain the NPL population and the interest accrued on it.
2. Test that suspension criteria were applied; reperform the suspended-interest calculation.
3. Verify accrued interest on NPLs is provided for or reversed per policy.

Population: Non-performing loans and accrued interest.

Sampling notes: Focus on newly classified NPLs and large exposures.

Expected result: Accrual stops per policy; uncollectible interest is provided for.

Exception criteria: Interest accruing on loans meeting suspension criteria; unprovided NPL interest.

Follow-up: Quantify the overstatement; propose reversal/provision; assess whether the policy itself is adequate.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Challenge classification and reperform valuations
description:
Objective: Test that instruments are correctly classified and fairly valued.

Technique: Reperformance

Steps: 1. Inspect classification decisions against the documented business model and contractual cash-flow characteristics.
2. For a sample of instruments, independently reperform or challenge the valuation model and its inputs.
3. Investigate period-end reclassifications.

Population: Treasury financial instruments.

Sampling notes: Focus on level 3 instruments and period-end reclassifications.

Expected result: Classifications follow the documented basis; valuations are within a reasonable range.

Exception criteria: Reclassifications without business-model change; valuations outside the auditor's range; unsupported unobservable inputs.

Follow-up: Develop an independent valuation range; propose adjustments; consider valuation-expert involvement.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Test fair value disclosures
description:
Objective: Verify hierarchy, sensitivity and technique disclosures.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Agree disclosed fair values and hierarchy levels to valuation outputs.
2. Verify sensitivity disclosures reflect stressed inputs.
3. Check valuation techniques are described.

Population: Fair value disclosures.

Sampling notes: Not applicable - full set.

Expected result: Disclosures agree and describe the techniques and sensitivities.

Exception criteria: Level 3 instruments disclosed as level 2; missing sensitivities.

Follow-up: Require corrected disclosure; evaluate the audit-report implication if refused.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Reconcile the inventory listing to the general ledger
description:
Objective: Confirm that the detailed inventory records agree with the general ledger balance that feeds the financial statements.

Technique: Recalculation

Steps: 1. Obtain the inventory listing (or inventory sub-ledger) as at the reporting date.
2. Foot and cross-foot the listing and agree the total to the general ledger inventory balance.
3. Investigate and obtain explanations for reconciling items; verify they are valid and recorded in the correct period.

Population: Full inventory listing and general ledger inventory accounts.

Sampling notes: No sampling - this is a full-population reconciliation.

Expected result: The inventory listing reconciles to the general ledger balance; reconciling items are valid, supported and recorded in the correct period.

Exception criteria: Unreconciled differences; reconciling items that are unsupported, stale, or recorded in the wrong period.

Follow-up: Investigate the cause of each unreconciled difference; quantify the potential misstatement; consider whether the difference indicates a breakdown in inventory record-keeping that warrants extended procedures.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Attend the physical inventory count and inspect selected items
description:
Objective: Obtain direct evidence of the existence and condition of inventory at the count date.

Technique: Observation

Steps: 1. Attend the entity's physical inventory count (where appropriate) and observe whether count procedures are followed.
2. Select a sample of inventory items and inspect their physical existence and condition.
3. Note the condition of storage, segregation of damaged or obsolete items, and any restrictions on access observed during attendance.

Population: Inventory on hand at the count date.

Sampling notes: Select items across locations and value strata, with emphasis on high-value and portable items given the security factor.

Expected result: Selected items exist, are in the expected location and condition, and count procedures appear to have been followed.

Exception criteria: Items selected cannot be located; significant quantities appear damaged or obsolete without segregation; count procedures are not followed.

Follow-up: Extend inspection to additional items; discuss findings with management; evaluate whether condition issues require valuation adjustments and whether count reliability is impaired.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Perform two-directional test counts
description:
Objective: Test both the existence of recorded inventory and the completeness of inventory records.

Technique: Physical verification

Steps: 1. From the inventory listing, select items and trace to their physical location (listing to floor) - tests existence.
2. From the warehouse floor, select items and trace back to the inventory listing (floor to listing) - tests completeness of records.
3. Record quantities independently and compare with both the listing and the entity's count sheets.

Population: Inventory listing and physical inventory on hand.

Sampling notes: Two-directional sample; bias selection toward high-value, portable items and locations with the weakest access controls.

Expected result: Test counts agree with the listing and count sheets, subject to individually investigated differences.

Exception criteria: Material unexplained differences in either direction; items on the floor not in the listing; listed items not on the floor.

Follow-up: Investigate each difference with warehouse staff; inspect movement records around the count date; if differences are material and unexplained, extend test counts and reassess the risk assessment for inventory.

title: Investigate material differences between physical counts and inventory records
description:
Objective: Determine the cause of count differences and whether adjustments are required.

Technique: Inquiry

Steps: 1. Obtain the entity's count-to-record reconciliation and identify material differences.
2. For each material difference, inspect supporting documentation (movement records, dispatch notes, receiving reports).
3. Discuss unexplained differences with warehouse and finance personnel and document explanations with corroborating evidence.

Population: All material count differences.

Sampling notes: Census of material differences; professional judgment for the materiality threshold.

Expected result: Each material difference is explained by valid, supported causes (e.g. timing of movements, data entry errors since corrected) and correctly adjusted.

Exception criteria: Material unexplained shortages; explanations without supporting evidence; a pattern of differences concentrated in high-value or portable lines.

Follow-up: Quantify the potential misstatement; consider extended procedures over the affected lines or locations; evaluate fraud risk indicators - do NOT automatically conclude fraud has occurred; document the basis for the conclusion.

title: Inspect inventory movement records around the count date
description:
Objective: Verify that movements around the count date are completely and accurately recorded so the count can be rolled forward or back to the reporting date.

Technique: Cut-off testing

Steps: 1. Obtain goods received notes and dispatch/delivery notes for a window around the count date.
2. Trace a sample of movements to the inventory records and vice versa.
3. Verify cut-off: movements before the reporting date are recorded in the correct period.

Population: Inventory movements in the window around the count date and year-end.

Sampling notes: Focus on the last/first movements of the period and on high-value items.

Expected result: Movements are completely recorded in the correct period; the count reconciles to the reporting-date balance.

Exception criteria: Missing movement records; movements recorded in the wrong period; unrecorded dispatches or receipts.

Follow-up: Quantify cut-off errors and propose adjustments; if movement records are systematically missing, extend testing and reconsider reliance on the entity's records.

title: Review adjustment journals relating to shortages and losses
description:
Objective: Verify that recorded inventory adjustments are valid, supported and correctly classified.

Technique: Vouching

Steps: 1. Extract all journals adjusting inventory for shortages, losses, damage or shrinkage in the period.
2. Inspect supporting documentation for each material adjustment.
3. Verify the accounting treatment: losses recognised in the correct period and classified appropriately (not netted against unrelated gains).

Population: All inventory adjustment journals in the period.

Sampling notes: Census of material adjustments; sample smaller ones if numerous.

Expected result: Adjustments are supported, approved, recorded in the correct period and correctly classified.

Exception criteria: Unsupported or unapproved adjustments; adjustments recorded in the wrong period; losses netted or misclassified to obscure shrinkage.

Follow-up: Investigate the business rationale for unsupported adjustments; quantify misstatements; consider whether the pattern indicates unrecorded losses elsewhere.

title: Inspect warehouse access records and investigate unusual movements
description:
Objective: Obtain evidence about who accessed inventory areas and whether movements were authorised.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Obtain access logs, key registers or entry records for the warehouse for the period (where available).
2. Identify unusual patterns: after-hours access, access by personnel without a business need, gaps in sequential logs.
3. Corroborate unusual movements with goods movement records and dispatch documentation.

Population: Warehouse access records for the period.

Sampling notes: Targeted review for anomalies rather than statistical sampling.

Expected result: Access is limited to authorised personnel; unusual movements are explained and supported by valid dispatch or transfer documentation.

Exception criteria: Evidence of unauthorised access; after-hours movements without supporting dispatch records; missing or tampered logs.

Follow-up: Investigate each anomaly with management; trace the related inventory; if unauthorised movements are confirmed, extend physical verification procedures and reassess fraud risk - without presuming fraud.

title: Evaluate whether discrepancies require accounting adjustments or additional procedures
description:
Objective: Conclude on the financial statement impact of all inventory findings taken together.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Aggregate all unadjusted differences, cut-off errors and unsupported adjustments identified.
2. Assess whether, individually or in aggregate, they indicate material misstatement of inventory or related accounts.
3. Determine whether additional audit procedures are needed and document the conclusion and its effect on the risk assessment.

Population: All inventory audit findings.

Sampling notes: Not applicable - this is an evaluation step.

Expected result: Findings are individually and in aggregate immaterial, or proposed adjustments have been recorded; the risk assessment remains appropriate.

Exception criteria: Aggregate unadjusted differences approach or exceed materiality; findings contradict the original risk assessment.

Follow-up: Propose adjustments to management; if refused, evaluate the impact on the audit opinion; update the risk assessment and extend procedures where the original assessment is no longer supported.

title: Analyse payroll cost trends by department and headcount
description:
Objective: Identify departments or periods where payroll cost is inconsistent with headcount, indicating possible payments to non-employees.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Obtain monthly payroll summaries and HR headcount reports for the period.
2. Compare payroll cost and headcount by department to prior periods and to budget.
3. Investigate departments where cost rises without corresponding headcount growth, or where payroll headcount exceeds HR headcount.

Population: Monthly payroll summaries and headcount reports for the period.

Sampling notes: Not sampling - trend analysis over the full period.

Expected result: Payroll cost movements are consistent with headcount changes and explained by valid causes (pay rises, headcount changes).

Exception criteria: Unexplained cost increases; headcount per payroll materially exceeding HR records; departments with cost growth but no headcount growth.

Follow-up: Drill into the affected department's payees; vouch a sample of employees to HR records; if ghost employees are indicated, extend procedures to quantify the overpayment and assess fraud risk indicators without presuming fraud.
