title: Trace leavers to removal from the payroll master
description:
Objective: Verify that terminated employees stop being paid after their last working day.

Technique: Tracing

Steps: 1. Obtain the HR leavers list for the period, with last working dates.
2. For a sample of leavers, inspect the payroll master to confirm the removal date precedes the next pay run.
3. Inspect the final pay calculation for each sampled leaver and agree it to the last working date.

Population: All employees who left in the period.

Sampling notes: Sample across months and departments; extend to a census if exceptions are found.

Expected result: Each leaver is removed from the payroll master before the next pay run; final pay is correctly calculated and supported.

Exception criteria: Leavers paid after their last working day; leavers still active in the master; final pay unsupported.

Follow-up: Quantify overpayments; investigate the cause; test whether overpaid amounts were recovered; consider extending testing to the full leaver population.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Vouch a sample of payees to current employment evidence
description:
Objective: Confirm that individuals paid through payroll are genuine current employees.

Technique: Vouching

Steps: 1. Select a sample of employees from the payroll register.
2. Vouch each to an HR employment file: appointment letter or contract, identification, and evidence of current employment (recent attendance, current supervisor).
3. Agree the bank account paid against the bank details held in the HR file.

Population: Payroll register for the period.

Sampling notes: Risk-based sample: include employees with no supervisor on record, recent bank detail changes, and round-sum net pay.

Expected result: Each sampled payee is a current employee supported by valid employment evidence, with bank details agreeing to HR records.

Exception criteria: Payees with no employment file; payees whose HR record shows termination; duplicate or suspicious bank account details shared between unrelated payees.

Follow-up: Investigate each exception with HR; quantify payments to the affected payees; evaluate fraud risk indicators - do not automatically conclude fraud; consider reporting obligations under professional standards.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Inspect the leaver-to-payroll process
description:
Objective: Test whether the leaver notification and removal control operates as designed.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Select a sample of terminations from the HR leavers list.
2. Inspect the leaver checklist for HR and payroll sign-off and dates.
3. For one case, reperform the check that removal preceded the next pay run.

Population: Terminations in the period.

Sampling notes: Sample across the period; include months with high leaver volumes.

Expected result: Checklists are complete, signed and dated; removals occur before the next pay run.

Exception criteria: Missing checklists; unsigned or late leaver notifications; removals processed after a further payment.

Follow-up: Control exceptions are control deficiencies, not proof of misstatement. Assess the deficiency and increase substantive procedures over leavers and payees accordingly.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Inspect payroll system access rights
description:
Objective: Determine whether system access enforces segregation between maintaining employee records and processing payments.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Obtain the payroll system user access report (extracted directly where possible).
2. Identify users holding both master-change and payment processing or release rights.
3. Inspect the most recent periodic access review for evidence of performance and follow-up.

Population: Payroll system users and access rights.

Sampling notes: Census of users with payroll permissions.

Expected result: No user combines incompatible duties; access reviews are performed and exceptions followed up.

Exception criteria: Users combining master-change and payment-release rights; access reviews missing, unsigned, or not followed up.

Follow-up: Treat as a control deficiency; do not conclude misstatement from access rights alone. Expand substantive procedures over master changes and payments for the period the weakness existed.

title: Vouch master changes to independent approval
description:
Objective: Verify that changes to employee master data are authorised and genuine.

Technique: Vouching

Steps: 1. Extract the audit trail of payroll master changes for the period.
2. Select a sample, covering all bank detail changes and new starters.
3. Vouch each change to an approved change request and to supporting HR documentation (appointment letter, contract amendment).

Population: All payroll master changes in the period (from the audit trail).

Sampling notes: Risk-based sample: all bank detail changes and new starters; sample of rate changes.

Expected result: Each sampled change is approved by an independent person before taking effect and supported by HR documentation.

Exception criteria: Unapproved changes; changes supported only by the person who entered them; bank detail changes without independent verification.

Follow-up: Investigate the business purpose of each unapproved change; trace the related payments; quantify any overpayment; evaluate fraud indicators without presuming fraud.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Reperform the payroll calculation for a sample of employees
description:
Objective: Verify the accuracy of payroll calculations for a sample of employees.

Technique: Recalculation

Steps: 1. Select a sample of employees from a recent pay run.
2. Independently recalculate gross pay, statutory and other deductions, and net pay from authorised rates and inputs.
3. Agree the bank details paid against the bank details in the HR file.

Population: Payroll register for a selected pay period.

Sampling notes: Sample across pay grades and departments; include employees with recent master changes.

Expected result: Recalculated gross pay, deductions and net pay agree with the payroll register.

Exception criteria: Differences in rates, hours or deductions; bank details differing from HR records.

Follow-up: Investigate whether differences indicate error or manipulation; if a pattern emerges, extend testing and reconsider the risk assessment.

title: Analyse new starters and bank detail changes
description:
Objective: Identify anomalous new payees or payment redirections indicative of fictitious employees.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Obtain lists of new starters and bank detail changes for the period.
2. Scan for anomalies: shared bank accounts, incomplete files, PO box or residential addresses inconsistent with the role, changes just before pay runs.
3. Vouch anomalies to HR employment evidence and approval records.

Population: New starters and bank detail changes in the period.

Sampling notes: Full-population scan for anomalies; targeted vouching of exceptions.

Expected result: All new starters and bank detail changes correspond to genuine employment events with complete documentation.

Exception criteria: Employees sharing bank accounts; new starters with incomplete files; bank detail changes clustered just before pay runs.

Follow-up: Vouch the anomalies to employment evidence; investigate with HR; if fictitious employees are indicated, quantify payments and assess fraud risk indicators without presuming fraud.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Vouch overtime payments to approved timesheets
description:
Objective: Verify that paid overtime was actually worked and independently approved.

Technique: Vouching

Steps: 1. Select a sample of overtime payments, weighted toward the highest earners.
2. Vouch each to the underlying timesheet and to independent supervisor approval.
3. Agree claimed hours to attendance or production records for the same dates.

Population: Overtime payments in the period.

Sampling notes: Risk-based sample: highest overtime earners and departments with spikes.

Expected result: Sampled overtime payments are supported by approved timesheets and corroborated by attendance records.

Exception criteria: Overtime paid without approval; approved hours differing from attendance records; overtime claimed by employees recorded as absent.

Follow-up: Quantify unapproved or uncorroborated overtime; investigate with supervisors; if the pattern is systemic, extend testing and consider the control deficiency in the risk assessment.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Analyse overtime trends and exceptions
description:
Objective: Identify unusual overtime patterns indicative of inflated claims.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Analyse overtime cost and hours by employee and department, compared to prior periods.
2. Identify concentrations, spikes and employees whose overtime is disproportionate to their role.
3. Corroborate explanations against production or activity records.

Population: Overtime cost by employee and department for the period and comparatives.

Sampling notes: Full-population analysis; threshold-based exception identification.

Expected result: Overtime patterns are consistent with operational needs and production levels; exceptions are explained.

Exception criteria: Overtime concentrated in a few employees without operational justification; spikes inconsistent with production levels.

Follow-up: Vouch unexplained exceptions to timesheets and approvals; investigate with operational management.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Recalculate overtime pay
description:
Objective: Verify overtime is calculated at the correct rates.

Technique: Recalculation

Steps: 1. Select a sample of overtime payments.
2. Independently recalculate overtime pay from approved hours and the authorised overtime rates.
3. Investigate differences.

Population: Overtime payments in a selected pay period.

Sampling notes: Sample covering different overtime rate bands.

Expected result: Recalculated overtime pay agrees with amounts paid.

Exception criteria: Overtime paid at incorrect rates; hours paid differing from approved hours.

Follow-up: Determine whether differences are isolated errors or systematic; quantify and propose adjustment if material.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Test the overtime approval control
description:
Objective: Test whether the overtime approval control operates as designed.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Select a sample of overtime claims.
2. Inspect each for approval by a supervisor independent of the claimant, dated before or promptly after payment.
3. Note any self-approved or missing approvals.

Population: Overtime claims in the period.

Sampling notes: Sample across departments and months.

Expected result: Overtime claims show timely approval by an independent supervisor.

Exception criteria: Claims paid without independent approval; approvals by the claimant's subordinate or peer.

Follow-up: A missing approval is a control deficiency, not proof the overtime was not worked. Increase substantive vouching of unapproved claims.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Recalculate net pay for a sample of employees
description:
Objective: Verify payroll calculations are mathematically correct and based on current parameters.

Technique: Recalculation

Steps: 1. Select a sample of employees from recent pay runs.
2. Independently recalculate gross pay, each deduction (tax, social security, other) and net pay using the authorised rates and the statutory tables in force.
3. Compare with the payroll register and investigate differences.

Population: Payroll register for selected pay periods.

Sampling notes: Sample across pay grades; include employees with complex deductions.

Expected result: Recalculated gross pay, deductions and net pay agree with the payroll register.

Exception criteria: Recalculated amounts differ from the register; outdated tax tables used; deductions omitted or miscalculated.

Follow-up: Determine whether errors are isolated or systematic; if systematic, quantify the aggregate effect on wages expense and statutory liabilities and consider the compliance implications.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Agree pay rates to authorised sources
description:
Objective: Verify that pay rates in the payroll system are authorised.

Technique: Vouching

Steps: 1. Select a sample of employees, including all recent pay rate changes.
2. Agree the rate in the payroll master to the employment contract or approved salary schedule.
3. Inspect approval for each rate change.

Population: Pay rates in the payroll master.

Sampling notes: Sample across grades; include all recent rate changes.

Expected result: Pay rates used agree with authorised contracts or salary schedules.

Exception criteria: Rates in the payroll system differing from contracts or salary schedules; unauthorised rate changes.

Follow-up: Investigate unauthorised rates; quantify the effect; determine whether the change indicates error or manipulation.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Reconcile payroll to the general ledger and investigate differences
description:
Objective: Confirm payroll postings to the ledger are complete and agree with the payroll register.

Technique: Reperformance

Steps: 1. Reperform the reconciliation of the payroll register totals to the general ledger payroll accounts for each pay period.
2. Investigate and obtain explanations for reconciling items.
3. Verify that year-end payroll accruals are supported and correctly measured.

Population: Payroll register totals and general ledger payroll accounts for each pay period.

Sampling notes: Full-period reconciliation; no sampling.

Expected result: The payroll register reconciles to the general ledger; reconciling items are valid and explained.

Exception criteria: Unexplained reconciling items; payroll journals posted directly to the ledger bypassing the payroll summary.

Follow-up: Investigate unreconciled differences; quantify the potential misstatement of wages expense and related liabilities.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Analytical review of payroll cost per head
description:
Objective: Corroborate overall payroll reasonableness against headcount and known pay changes.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Calculate average payroll cost per head by department for the current and comparative periods.
2. Compare movements with known pay rises, headcount changes and overtime trends.
3. Investigate inconsistencies.

Population: Aggregate payroll cost and headcount for the period and comparatives.

Sampling notes: Not applicable - analytical review of aggregates.

Expected result: Average payroll cost per head is consistent with headcount changes, pay rises and the mix of employees.

Exception criteria: Average cost per head moving inconsistently with known pay rises or headcount changes; unexplained jumps in a single period.

Follow-up: Investigate unexplained movements by drilling into the underlying payees and rates.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Test the classification of repairs and maintenance expenditure
description:
Objective: Determine whether expenditure near the repairs-versus-capital boundary has been correctly classified.

Technique: Vouching

Steps: 1. Obtain the repairs and maintenance expense ledger and the capital additions listing for the period.
2. Select items near the capitalisation boundary: large refurbishments, overhauls, year-end additions and vaguely described items.
3. For each selected item, inspect the supplier invoice and work description to establish the nature of the work performed.
4. Evaluate whether the expenditure meets the entity's capitalisation criteria (enhancement of future economic benefits beyond the originally assessed standard of performance) or is a repair.
5. Verify that capitalised items were approved and that the accounting treatment is consistent with similar items.

Population: Repairs and maintenance expense and capital additions for the period.

Sampling notes: Targeted selection: large or round-sum items, refurbishments, year-end additions, and items with vague descriptions; supplement with a random sample if the population is large.

Expected result: Each tested item is correctly classified: capitalised items meet the recognition criteria and are supported and approved; repairs are expensed.

Exception criteria: Expenditure capitalised that does not meet the capitalisation criteria; repairs of a capital nature left in expense; inconsistent treatment of similar items.

Follow-up: Quantify the misclassified amounts and propose adjustments; if misclassification is pervasive, extend testing across the additions and repairs populations and reconsider the risk assessment. Do not assume intent - errors and bias require different responses.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Inspect the capitalisation policy and test approval controls
description:
Objective: Establish the criteria the entity claims to apply and test whether approval controls operated.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Inspect the entity's capitalisation policy for clarity on repairs, replacements and major maintenance.
2. Select a sample of capital expenditure approval forms and verify they were completed before recognition and authorised independently of the requestor.
3. Check that the forms evidence consideration of the capitalisation criteria, not just budget approval.
4. Note instances where expenditure was recognised without approval as control exceptions.

Population: Capitalisation policy and capital expenditure approvals in the period.

Sampling notes: Inspect the policy in full; test a sample of approval forms across the period.

Expected result: A clear, approved policy exists that addresses the repairs-versus-capital boundary, and tested transactions are consistent with it.

Exception criteria: No written policy; policy unclear on the repairs boundary; evidence that the policy is not followed in practice.

Follow-up: Where the policy is absent or unclear, treat the classification risk as higher and extend substantive testing; discuss the gap with management as a control deficiency.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Perform analytical procedures over repairs and maintenance expense
description:
Objective: Identify unusual patterns in repairs expenditure that may indicate misclassification.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Develop an expectation for repairs and maintenance expense based on prior periods, the size and age of the asset base, and activity levels.
2. Compare actual expense to the expectation and investigate significant variances.
3. Compare the trend in repairs expense with the trend in capital additions for offsetting movements.
4. Corroborate explanations with operational evidence, not inquiry alone.

Population: Repairs and maintenance expense by month and by asset class, with capital additions for comparison.

Sampling notes: Not a sampling procedure; set an investigation threshold based on materiality.

Expected result: Repairs and maintenance expense is consistent with expectations given the asset base, activity levels and prior periods; significant variances are explained and corroborated.

Exception criteria: Repairs expense significantly below expectation without a convincing operational explanation; a shift of expenditure from repairs into additions.

Follow-up: Investigate unexplained variances by selecting the underlying items for vouching; a persistent, unexplained decline in repairs expense alongside rising additions indicates higher classification risk.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Recalculate depreciation for a sample of assets
description:
Objective: Verify the arithmetical accuracy of the depreciation charge.

Technique: Recalculation

Steps: 1. Obtain the fixed asset register with cost, depreciation rate, method and useful life by asset.
2. Independently recalculate the depreciation charge for each sampled asset, including part-year calculations for additions and disposals.
3. Compare the recalculation with the recorded charge and investigate differences.
4. Agree the approved parameters used to the depreciation policy and any authorised changes.

Population: Depreciation charge for the period by asset.

Sampling notes: Sample across asset classes and acquisition years; include assets added and disposed of in the period (part-year calculations).

Expected result: The recalculated depreciation charge agrees with the recorded charge for each sampled asset, using the approved rate, method and useful life.

Exception criteria: Recalculated charge differs materially from the recorded charge; incorrect rates, lives or methods applied to sampled assets.

Follow-up: Investigate the cause of each difference (data error, wrong parameter, formula fault); quantify the effect across the population; if parameters were wrong, refer to the evaluation of useful lives.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Evaluate the appropriateness of useful lives and depreciation methods
description:
Objective: Assess whether the depreciation parameters themselves are appropriate, not just accurately applied.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Inspect management's documented review of useful lives, methods and residual values.
2. Challenge the conclusions: compare lives with actual asset usage and condition, technological change, and industry practice.
3. Investigate warning signs such as fully depreciated assets still in active use or lives extended without documented justification.
4. Evaluate whether changes in estimates have been accounted for prospectively and disclosed where required.

Population: Depreciation policies, lives and methods by asset class.

Sampling notes: Focus on material asset classes and on classes showing warning signs (e.g. fully depreciated assets still in use).

Expected result: Useful lives, methods and residual values are reasonable and consistent with how the assets are used, their condition, and observable technological or market change.

Exception criteria: Useful lives or methods that are not supportable given asset usage, condition, technological change or industry practice; lives extended without justification.

Follow-up: Where lives are not supportable, estimate the effect of reasonable lives on the charge and carrying amount; discuss with management and consider a control deficiency where the review process failed.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Test authorisation of changes to depreciation parameters
description:
Objective: Test whether changes to depreciation parameters are controlled.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Extract the log of changes to depreciation parameters in the asset master data for the period.
2. For each selected change, inspect the authorisation and the documented rationale.
3. Verify the authoriser was independent of the person requesting or entering the change.
4. Confirm the change was applied from the correct date.

Population: All changes to depreciation rates, methods or useful lives in the period.

Sampling notes: Census of changes if few; sample if numerous, weighted toward changes reducing the charge.

Expected result: All changes to depreciation parameters in the period were independently authorised, documented and logged.

Exception criteria: Changes to rates, methods or lives made without independent authorisation or without documentation; unauthorised access to asset master data.

Follow-up: Treat unauthorised changes as control exceptions; establish who made them and why; extend testing to the affected assets' charges.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Physically verify a sample of assets from the register
description:
Objective: Obtain direct evidence that recorded assets still exist.

Technique: Physical verification

Steps: 1. Select a sample of assets from the fixed asset register.
2. Locate each sampled asset physically and confirm its identity (asset tag, serial number or description).
3. Note the asset's location and apparent condition, and any discrepancies with the register.
4. For assets that cannot be located, record the details for follow-up investigation.

Population: Fixed asset register at the reporting date.

Sampling notes: Sample across locations and asset classes, weighted toward portable, high-value and older assets; include some fully depreciated assets.

Expected result: Each sampled asset exists, is identifiable, and is in the recorded location and apparent condition.

Exception criteria: Selected assets that cannot be located; assets found in a substantially different condition or location from the records.

Follow-up: Investigate each missing asset: confirm whether it was disposed of, scrapped, transferred or stolen; if disposed of, verify the accounting treatment; a pattern of missing assets indicates the register is unreliable and testing must be extended.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Inspect disposal records and verify the accounting for disposals
description:
Objective: Verify that recorded disposals are genuine, authorised and correctly accounted for.

Technique: Vouching

Steps: 1. Obtain the listing of disposals recorded in the period.
2. For each selected disposal, inspect the disposal authorisation form and confirm it predates or coincides with the disposal.
3. Trace proceeds to supporting records (sales invoices, weighbridge tickets, bank receipts).
4. Recalculate the gain or loss on disposal and verify the asset was removed from the register and ledger in the correct period.

Population: All disposals recorded in the period.

Sampling notes: Census of material disposals; sample smaller ones.

Expected result: Each tested disposal was authorised, completely removed from the register and ledger in the correct period, and the gain or loss correctly calculated.

Exception criteria: Disposals without authorisation; proceeds that do not agree to supporting records; gains or losses incorrectly calculated; derecognition in the wrong period.

Follow-up: Quantify misstatements in gains, losses and carrying amounts; investigate unauthorised disposals with management; consider whether missing authorisations indicate a wider control failure.

title: Search for unrecorded disposals
description:
Objective: Detect disposals that occurred but were never recorded.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Review board minutes and operational reports for mention of asset sales, scrapping, demolitions or site closures.
2. Compare insurance schedules and, where available, tax asset listings with the fixed asset register for assets that have disappeared.
3. Inspect bank receipts and sales records for disposal proceeds with no matching derecognition.
4. Follow up each indication with operations and finance staff and inspect the register treatment.

Population: Board minutes, insurance schedules, proceeds records and operational reports for the period.

Sampling notes: Targeted search rather than statistical sampling; focus on asset-intensive operations and sites with turnover of equipment.

Expected result: No material unrecorded disposals are identified; where identified, they are quantified and adjusted.

Exception criteria: Evidence of disposals (board minutes, insurance changes, proceeds) with no corresponding derecognition; assets known to have been scrapped still on the register.

Follow-up: Quantify the carrying amount of unrecorded disposals and propose adjustments; report the communication breakdown between operations and finance as a control deficiency.

title: Evaluate management's impairment indicator assessment
description:
Objective: Evaluate whether management's impairment indicator assessment is complete and reasonable.

Technique: Inquiry

Steps: 1. Inspect management's documented assessment of impairment indicators, covering internal sources (obsolescence, damage, underperformance, idleness) and external sources (market declines, technological, regulatory or economic change).
2. Inquire of operational and finance management about asset performance, idle capacity and market developments.
3. Compare the assessment against the auditor's own knowledge from other audit work (site visits, analytical procedures, board minutes).
4. Document indicators identified by the auditor that management omitted.

Population: Management's impairment indicator assessment at the reporting date.

Sampling notes: Not a sampling procedure; covers the assessment as a whole, focused on material assets and cash-generating units.

Expected result: Management's assessment addresses the relevant internal and external indicator categories and its conclusion is consistent with the auditor's own observations.

Exception criteria: Indicators exist that management's assessment did not consider; assessment is undocumented or perfunctory.

Follow-up: Where indicators were missed, perform the auditor's own indicator assessment and, where indicators exist, require or perform impairment testing; treat a perfunctory assessment as a control deficiency.

title: Perform analytical procedures to identify impairment indicators
description:
Objective: Use analytical procedures to independently identify possible impairment indicators.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Analyse trends in revenue, margins and utilisation for significant assets or cash-generating units against budgets and prior periods.
2. Compare carrying amounts with observable market data for similar assets where available.
3. Consider external information: industry downturns, technological change, regulatory developments.
4. Investigate adverse variances and trends with management, corroborating explanations.

Population: Asset-level or cash-generating-unit performance data, market data and industry information.

Sampling notes: Not a sampling procedure; set investigation thresholds with regard to materiality.

Expected result: Analytical procedures either identify no indicators of impairment, or the indicators identified are consistent with those management has addressed.

Exception criteria: Significant adverse trends or variances that indicate possible impairment and have not been addressed by management.

Follow-up: Investigate each unaddressed indicator; where it suggests an asset may be impaired, proceed to testing of the recoverable amount.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Inspect impairment tests and challenge key assumptions
description:
Objective: Test the impairment measurement where indicators of impairment exist.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Where indicators exist, obtain management's impairment test (value in use or fair value less costs of disposal).
2. Evaluate the reasonableness of key assumptions: cash flow forecasts, growth rates, discount rates - and their consistency with other audit evidence.
3. Test the mathematical accuracy of the model and the completeness of the cash-generating unit's carrying amount.
4. Verify that any impairment loss is recognised in the correct period and that required disclosures are made.

Population: Assets or cash-generating units where impairment indicators have been identified.

Sampling notes: Census of material assets/CGUs with indicators; judgmental selection below materiality.

Expected result: Where indicators exist, an impairment test has been performed using supportable assumptions, and any required impairment loss (and related disclosures) is recognised.

Exception criteria: Recoverable amount below carrying amount with no impairment recognised; key assumptions that are not supportable or inconsistent with other audit evidence.

Follow-up: Challenge unsupported assumptions and quantify the effect of reasonable alternatives; propose adjustments for unrecognised impairment; evaluate the implications for the audit opinion if management refuses.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Inspect replacement work orders and verify derecognition of replaced parts
description:
Objective: Verify that replaced significant components have been derecognised.

Technique: Vouching

Steps: 1. Obtain the listing of capitalised replacement and major maintenance expenditure for the period.
2. For each selected item, inspect the work order to identify the component replaced and the nature of the work.
3. Trace the item to the fixed asset register and verify that the replaced component's carrying amount was derecognised at the same time the new cost was recognised.
4. Where the replaced part was not separately identified, evaluate the reasonableness of management's estimate of its carrying amount.

Population: Major maintenance, overhaul and replacement work orders capitalised in the period.

Sampling notes: Targeted selection of the largest replacement programmes and overhauls; census where few.

Expected result: For each tested replacement, the replaced component has been derecognised (or its carrying amount estimated and removed where it was not separately identified), and only the new cost remains capitalised.

Exception criteria: Replacement expenditure capitalised with no derecognition of the replaced part; replaced part's carrying amount unknown because it was never separately identified.

Follow-up: Quantify the double-counted carrying amount and propose adjustments; where components were never separately identified, evaluate whether estimation of the replaced part's carrying amount is required; report the information-flow gap as a control deficiency.

title: Test componentisation of significant assets
description:
Objective: Test whether significant assets are appropriately componentised.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Identify significant assets with major parts that have different useful lives or consumption patterns.
2. Inspect the register to confirm those parts are recorded as separate components with their own depreciation parameters.
3. Evaluate the reasonableness of the significance judgments and the allocated costs.
4. Consider the implications for depreciation accuracy and for future derecognition.

Population: Significant assets recognised or revalued in the period, and major asset classes.

Sampling notes: Focus on high-value, complex assets (plant, buildings, aircraft, networks).

Expected result: Significant assets are componentised with major parts separately identified and depreciated over their own useful lives.

Exception criteria: Significant assets recorded as single lines with no component breakdown; major parts with materially different useful lives depreciated as one.

Follow-up: Where componentisation is absent, assess whether the resulting depreciation and derecognition errors could be material; discuss the gap with management.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Observe significant replacement work
description:
Objective: Corroborate the nature of replacement work through direct observation.

Technique: Observation

Steps: 1. Identify significant replacement or overhaul work in progress or recently completed.
2. Observe the work and the components involved, noting what is being replaced.
3. Compare observations with the work order descriptions and the register treatment.
4. Document the corroboration obtained for the derecognition conclusions.

Population: Major replacement or overhaul work in progress or recently completed.

Sampling notes: Judgmental selection of accessible, significant replacement work.

Expected result: The physical work observed is consistent with the work orders tested, supporting the accounting for replacements and derecognitions.

Exception criteria: Work performed does not match the work order description; replaced components still recorded as in use.

Follow-up: Investigate inconsistencies between observed work and recorded work orders; extend inspection where descriptions appear unreliable.

title: Vouch purchase invoices to goods received notes and purchase orders
description:
Objective: Verify that recorded purchases are supported by evidence of receipt.

Technique: Vouching

Steps: 1. Select a sample of purchase invoices across the period.
2. For each, inspect the matched purchase order and goods received note.
3. Verify quantities, prices and supplier details agree across documents.
4. Investigate invoices with no matching GRN or with mismatched details.

Population: Purchase invoices recorded in the period.

Sampling notes: Stratify by value; include a mix of suppliers; bias toward invoices approved without a visible match.

Expected result: Each sampled invoice is matched to a valid GRN and purchase order with consistent details.

Exception criteria: Invoices with no GRN; quantity or price mismatches; GRNs dated after the invoice without explanation.

Follow-up: Investigate whether exceptions represent missing documents or invalid purchases; quantify potential overstatement; extend testing if a pattern emerges.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Reperform the three-way matching control
description:
Objective: Test whether the matching control operated effectively through the period.

Technique: Reperformance

Steps: 1. Select a sample of paid invoices.
2. Reperform the match: verify purchase order, GRN and invoice agreed before payment was released.
3. Note any payments released without a complete match.
4. Conclude on control operation.

Population: Invoices subject to the matching control.

Sampling notes: Sample across the period; no deviations expected if reliance is planned.

Expected result: The control operated without deviation.

Exception criteria: Payments released without a complete three-way match; evidence of override.

Follow-up: A failed control test does not prove purchases are misstated - extend substantive vouching to establish whether invalid purchases were actually recorded; reassess control risk.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Inspect the unmatched-invoices exception report
description:
Objective: Verify that invoices paid without matching evidence were valid and followed up.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Obtain the exception report of invoices approved without matching GRNs.
2. Inspect the independent review and follow-up documented.
3. For a sample of items, inspect the alternative evidence of receipt obtained.
4. Assess whether unresolved items indicate invalid purchases.

Population: Exception report items for the period.

Sampling notes: Focus on high-value and long-outstanding items.

Expected result: All exceptions were independently reviewed and resolved with valid evidence of receipt.

Exception criteria: Unreviewed exceptions; items cleared without evidence; long-outstanding unmatched invoices.

Follow-up: Investigate unresolved items as potential invalid purchases; quantify exposure; consider implications for the control environment.

title: Trace pre-year-end goods received notes to the purchase ledger
description:
Objective: Detect liabilities for goods received but not recorded at year-end.

Technique: Tracing

Steps: 1. Obtain the sequential GRN register for the window before the reporting date.
2. Select GRNs and trace each to the purchase ledger or the year-end accrual.
3. Verify the liability was recorded in the correct period.
4. List unmatched GRNs and agree them to accrual journals.

Population: GRNs in the window before the reporting date.

Sampling notes: Focus on the final days before year-end and high-value receipts.

Expected result: All selected GRNs are recorded as purchases or accrued liabilities in the correct period.

Exception criteria: GRNs with no matching purchase or accrual; accruals unsupported by GRNs.

Follow-up: Propose accrual adjustments for unrecorded liabilities; quantify the understatement; assess whether the accrual process needs extended testing.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Test post-year-end purchase invoices for pre-year-end receipt
description:
Objective: Verify that invoices recorded after year-end do not hide pre-year-end liabilities.

Technique: Cut-off testing

Steps: 1. Select purchase invoices recorded in the first weeks after the reporting date.
2. Inspect the related GRN dates.
3. Where goods were received before year-end, verify an accrual was recorded.
4. Aggregate with pre-year-end direction testing.

Population: Purchase invoices recorded shortly after the reporting date.

Sampling notes: Cover at least two to four weeks after year-end.

Expected result: Post-year-end invoices relate to post-year-end receipts, or pre-year-end receipts were accrued.

Exception criteria: Invoices for pre-year-end receipts recorded only after year-end with no accrual.

Follow-up: Propose cut-off adjustments; extend the post-year-end window if errors indicate a systematic problem.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Inspect the year-end accrual for unmatched goods received
description:
Objective: Verify that management's accrual for uninvoiced receipts is complete and supported.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Obtain the year-end accrual schedule for unmatched GRNs.
2. Test the completeness of the GRN population used.
3. Agree a sample of accrued items to GRNs and subsequent invoices.
4. Assess whether the accrual basis (quantities, prices) is reasonable.

Population: The year-end GRN accrual.

Sampling notes: Test the schedule as a whole; sample accrued items for agreement to GRNs.

Expected result: The accrual is complete, supported by GRNs and recorded at appropriate amounts.

Exception criteria: Incomplete GRN population; accrued items without GRN support; unreasonable pricing assumptions.

Follow-up: Perform independent completeness testing where the schedule cannot be relied upon; propose adjustments for unsupported amounts.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Inspect the supplier master change log and approvals
description:
Objective: Test whether changes to supplier master data were independently approved.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Obtain the supplier master change log for the period.
2. Select a sample of changes, including all changes to bank details.
3. Inspect evidence of independent approval and supporting verification.
4. Identify changes made by users who also process payments.

Population: Supplier master changes in the period.

Sampling notes: Census of bank-detail changes; sample other changes.

Expected result: All sampled changes were independently approved with supporting verification documents.

Exception criteria: Unapproved changes; changes approved by the requestor; missing verification documents.

Follow-up: Unapproved changes are control deviations, not proof of fraud: investigate the business reason, verify the supplier's legitimacy, and vouch related payments; extend testing if deviations are systemic.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Vouch payments to newly added or changed suppliers
description:
Objective: Verify that payments to new or changed suppliers relate to genuine business transactions.

Technique: Vouching

Steps: 1. Identify suppliers added or changed during the period.
2. Select payments made to those suppliers.
3. Vouch each payment to the purchase order, GRN and invoice.
4. Verify the supplier's legitimacy through independent evidence (for example, business registration or verified contact details).

Population: Payments to suppliers added or changed in the period.

Sampling notes: Bias toward suppliers with limited trading history and large first payments.

Expected result: Payments are supported by genuine purchase documentation and the supplier is independently verifiable.

Exception criteria: Payments without supporting purchase evidence; suppliers that cannot be independently verified.

Follow-up: Investigate unverifiable suppliers thoroughly; trace the flow of funds where possible; if diversion is suspected, treat as a fraud indicator and consider the need for forensic expertise - do not conclude fraud has occurred.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Analyse the supplier master for indicators of fictitious suppliers
description:
Objective: Detect anomalies in supplier master data suggesting fictitious entries.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Obtain the full supplier master file.
2. Analyse for duplicate bank accounts, duplicate addresses, PO box addresses, and suppliers sharing employee addresses or contact details.
3. Flag suppliers with no purchase history but with payments, and round-sum payment patterns.
4. Investigate flagged suppliers with corroborating evidence.

Population: Full supplier master file.

Sampling notes: Full-population analysis; judgemental investigation of flagged items.

Expected result: Flagged items are explained by genuine business reasons with supporting evidence.

Exception criteria: Multiple suppliers sharing bank details; suppliers unverifiable through independent sources.

Follow-up: Subject flagged suppliers to detailed vouching and verification; treat persistent anomalies as fraud risk indicators.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Use data analysis to identify potential duplicate invoices
description:
Objective: Detect invoices that may have been recorded more than once.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Obtain the full purchase ledger for the period.
2. Analyse for duplicate combinations of supplier, invoice number, date and amount, and for near-duplicates with altered invoice numbers.
3. Select potential duplicates for detailed testing.
4. Distinguish genuine reissued invoices from double recordings.

Population: Full purchase ledger.

Sampling notes: Full-population analysis.

Expected result: Potential duplicates are explained (for example, genuine reissued invoices with credit notes) or confirmed as isolated errors.

Exception criteria: Confirmed double recordings; duplicate payments identified.

Follow-up: Quantify double-recorded purchases and duplicate payments; investigate the control breakdown; propose adjustments and recovery of duplicate payments.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Vouch suspected duplicate invoices to invoice copies and payment records
description:
Objective: Establish whether suspected duplicates are genuine double recordings.

Technique: Vouching

Steps: 1. For each suspected duplicate, obtain the supplier invoice copies.
2. Compare invoice numbers, dates, amounts and supporting GRNs.
3. Inspect payment records to determine whether both entries were paid.
4. Conclude whether a duplicate recording or duplicate payment occurred.

Population: Suspected duplicate invoices flagged by data analysis.

Sampling notes: All flagged items above a de minimis threshold.

Expected result: Each suspected duplicate is resolved: either a genuine separate invoice or a confirmed duplicate with quantified effect.

Exception criteria: Confirmed duplicate recordings; duplicate payments made.

Follow-up: Propose adjustments for overstated purchases and payables; follow up on recovery of duplicate payments from suppliers.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Inspect whether paid invoices are marked to prevent reprocessing
description:
Objective: Test the control preventing paid invoices re-entering the payment process.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Select a sample of paid invoices.
2. Inspect whether each is marked as paid (stamp, system flag) and filed appropriately.
3. Consider whether any paid invoice could be reprocessed.
4. Conclude on control operation.

Population: Paid invoices in the period.

Sampling notes: Sample across the period and across processing staff.

Expected result: Paid invoices are consistently marked and controlled against reprocessing.

Exception criteria: Unmarked paid invoices; invoices accessible for reprocessing.

Follow-up: Where the control fails, extend substantive duplicate testing; a failed control test alone does not prove duplicates exist.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Test purchase cut-off around the reporting date
description:
Objective: Verify purchases are recorded in the period the goods were received.

Technique: Cut-off testing

Steps: 1. Select purchase invoices from the last days before and first days after the reporting date.
2. Compare invoice dates with GRN dates.
3. Select GRNs from the same window and trace to the purchase ledger.
4. Investigate items where invoice and receipt dates fall in different periods.

Population: Purchase invoices and GRNs around the reporting date.

Sampling notes: Both directions; extend the window if processing backlogs exist.

Expected result: Purchases are recorded in the period of receipt; no material cut-off errors.

Exception criteria: Purchases recorded by invoice date in a different period from receipt.

Follow-up: Quantify cut-off errors and propose adjustments; if systematic, extend testing and reassess the period-end process.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Trace goods received notes to the purchase ledger for completeness
description:
Objective: Verify that all goods received are recorded as purchases.

Technique: Tracing

Steps: 1. Select GRNs from across the period, with emphasis on period end.
2. Trace each to the purchase ledger.
3. Verify quantities and amounts recorded agree with the GRN.
4. Follow up on GRNs with no matching purchase.

Population: GRNs across the period.

Sampling notes: Emphasis on period end; include high-value receipts.

Expected result: All selected GRNs are recorded completely and accurately.

Exception criteria: GRNs with no matching purchase; quantity or amount differences.

Follow-up: Investigate unrecorded GRNs; propose adjustments; consider whether the pattern indicates a completeness problem requiring extended procedures.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Analyse monthly purchase trends for cut-off anomalies
description:
Objective: Identify unusual purchase patterns suggesting cut-off errors.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Compare monthly purchases and payables with prior periods and budgets.
2. Investigate months with unusual spikes or troughs, especially around period ends.
3. Correlate with inventory movements and operational data.
4. Corroborate explanations with documentary evidence.

Population: Monthly purchase data for the period.

Sampling notes: Full-period analysis.

Expected result: Trends are consistent with operational activity; variances explained and corroborated.

Exception criteria: Unexplained period-end spikes or troughs inconsistent with operations.

Follow-up: Direct cut-off testing at the months flagged; analytical exceptions alone are not misstatements.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Vouch recorded sales to evidence that recognition criteria were met
description:
Objective: Verify that recorded sales represent genuine revenue earned in the period.

Technique: Vouching

Steps: 1. Select a sample of sales invoices, biasing selection toward period-end and large or unusual transactions.
2. For each sampled invoice, inspect the matched dispatch note, delivery record or service completion evidence and customer acceptance where applicable.
3. Compare dates: confirm the recognition event occurred on or before the invoice date.
4. Investigate any invoice dated before its supporting evidence or lacking evidence.

Population: Sales invoices recorded in the period.

Sampling notes: Bias toward the last month of the period and high-value or unusual items; stratify by revenue stream if streams have different recognition triggers.

Expected result: Each sampled sale is supported by dispatch or acceptance evidence dated on or before the invoice date.

Exception criteria: Invoices dated before the related dispatch or acceptance; missing, backdated or inconsistent supporting evidence.

Follow-up: Quantify the premature revenue; investigate the cause, including whether side agreements exist; extend the sample if exceptions suggest a pattern; where indicators point to possible deliberate misstatement, treat them as fraud risk indicators and extend procedures - do not conclude fraud has occurred.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Inspect contracts and terms for selected revenue transactions
description:
Objective: Confirm that the accounting treatment of selected transactions matches their contractual terms.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Select a sample of material or non-standard sales, including any bill-and-hold style arrangements.
2. Inspect the underlying contracts or sales orders to identify performance obligations, delivery and acceptance terms.
3. Compare the terms with the timing and amount of revenue recognised.
4. Document any side agreements or modified terms and assess their effect.

Population: Material and non-standard revenue transactions.

Sampling notes: Targeted selection, not statistical sampling: focus on complex terms, bill-and-hold claims and new customer arrangements.

Expected result: Revenue recognised is consistent with the contractual performance obligations and acceptance terms.

Exception criteria: Revenue recognised before contractual conditions are met; undisclosed side agreements; terms inconsistent with the invoice.

Follow-up: Reassess the revenue recognised on affected transactions; investigate the business rationale for side agreements; consider the implications for the fraud risk assessment without presuming fraud.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Test revenue cut-off around the reporting date
description:
Objective: Verify that sales are recorded in the correct accounting period.

Technique: Cut-off testing

Steps: 1. Select sales invoices from the last days before and first days after the reporting date.
2. Trace each to the related dispatch or completion evidence and compare dates.
3. Select dispatch notes from the same window and trace to the sales ledger to test completeness of recording.
4. Investigate items where invoice and dispatch dates fall in different periods.

Population: Sales invoices and dispatch notes in a window around the reporting date.

Sampling notes: Cover both directions (ledger to dispatch, dispatch to ledger); extend the window if the entity has invoicing backlogs.

Expected result: Sales are recorded in the period in which the recognition event occurred; no material cut-off errors.

Exception criteria: Invoices recorded in a different period from the dispatch or completion event; unmatched dispatches from before year-end.

Follow-up: Quantify cut-off errors and propose adjustments; if backlogs are systematic, extend testing and reconsider reliance on the entity's period-end procedures.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Reperform the billing-to-dispatch matching control
description:
Objective: Test whether the control preventing billing without dispatch evidence operated effectively.

Technique: Reperformance

Steps: 1. Select a sample of sales invoices from the period.
2. Reperform the matching control: verify that each invoice was matched to dispatch evidence before release.
3. Note any invoices released without a match or with perfunctory matching.
4. Conclude on whether the control operated throughout the period.

Population: Sales invoices subject to the matching control.

Sampling notes: Sample across the period, including period-end; smaller samples may support a controls-reliance strategy only if no deviations are found.

Expected result: The control operated without deviation: every sampled invoice was matched to valid dispatch evidence before billing.

Exception criteria: Deviations where invoices were released without matching evidence; evidence of override.

Follow-up: A failed control test does not prove revenue is misstated - extend substantive procedures (vouching, cut-off testing) to determine whether misstatements actually occurred; reassess control risk.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Trace pre-year-end dispatch notes to the sales ledger
description:
Objective: Detect sales earned before year-end that were not recorded in the correct period.

Technique: Tracing

Steps: 1. Obtain the sequential dispatch register for a window before the reporting date.
2. Select dispatch notes and trace each to the sales ledger.
3. Verify the sale was recorded in the period of dispatch.
4. List unmatched dispatches and follow up on their recording.

Population: Dispatch notes in the window before the reporting date.

Sampling notes: Focus on the final days before year-end; include high-value dispatches.

Expected result: All selected dispatches are recorded as sales in the correct period.

Exception criteria: Dispatches with no matching sale, or sales recorded in a later period.

Follow-up: Quantify unrecorded or late-recorded sales; propose accrual adjustments; investigate whether the backlog indicates a breakdown in period-end procedures.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Test post-year-end sales for pre-year-end dispatch
description:
Objective: Verify that sales recorded after year-end do not belong to the current period.

Technique: Cut-off testing

Steps: 1. Select sales invoices recorded in the first weeks after the reporting date.
2. Inspect the related dispatch or completion evidence and dates.
3. Where dispatch occurred before year-end, verify the sale was accrued in the correct period.
4. Aggregate findings with the pre-year-end direction testing.

Population: Sales recorded shortly after the reporting date.

Sampling notes: Cover at least two to four weeks after year-end, longer if invoicing backlogs are known.

Expected result: Post-year-end sales relate to post-year-end dispatches, or pre-year-end dispatches were correctly accrued.

Exception criteria: Sales relating to pre-year-end dispatch recorded only after year-end with no accrual.

Follow-up: Propose cut-off adjustments; extend the post-year-end window if errors are found.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Inspect the period-end dispatch-to-invoice reconciliation
description:
Objective: Verify that management's own cut-off reconciliation is complete and supported.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Obtain management's reconciliation of dispatch records to sales invoices at the reporting date.
2. Inspect the completeness of the dispatch population used.
3. Test a sample of unmatched items to accrual journals or subsequent invoices.
4. Assess whether reconciling items are valid and recorded in the correct period.

Population: The period-end dispatch-to-invoice reconciliation.

Sampling notes: Not a sampling exercise over transactions; test the reconciliation as a whole and sample its reconciling items.

Expected result: The reconciliation is complete; unmatched dispatches are validly accrued or explained.

Exception criteria: Incomplete dispatch population; unsupported or stale reconciling items; unmatched dispatches with no accrual.

Follow-up: Perform independent cut-off testing where the reconciliation cannot be relied upon; quantify the effect of unsupported items.

title: Vouch sales invoices to dispatch and order evidence
description:
Objective: Verify that recorded sales are supported by genuine underlying transactions.

Technique: Vouching

Steps: 1. Select a sample of sales invoices across the period.
2. For each, inspect the customer order and the matched dispatch note or proof of delivery.
3. Verify customer details, quantities and prices agree across documents.
4. Investigate invoices with no supporting evidence.

Population: Credit sales invoices recorded in the period.

Sampling notes: Include a mix of routine and unusual items; bias toward customers with no prior trading history.

Expected result: Each sampled invoice is supported by a matching order and dispatch evidence with consistent details.

Exception criteria: Invoices with no dispatch evidence; mismatched quantities, prices or customer details.

Follow-up: Investigate whether unsupported invoices represent fictitious sales or missing documents; extend testing if a pattern emerges; treat persistent unsupported items as fraud risk indicators without presuming fraud.

title: Analyse revenue against dispatch volumes and trends
description:
Objective: Identify unusual revenue patterns that may indicate unsupported or premature sales.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Compare recorded revenue with dispatch volumes or other operational data by month.
2. Investigate months where revenue diverges from operational activity.
3. Compare gross margins and revenue growth with prior periods and expectations.
4. Corroborate explanations for significant variances with documentary evidence.

Population: Monthly revenue and related operational data.

Sampling notes: Not applicable - analytical procedures cover the full population of monthly data.

Expected result: Revenue trends are consistent with dispatch volumes and operational activity; variances are explained and corroborated.

Exception criteria: Unexplained divergences between revenue and dispatch activity; unusual period-end spikes.

Follow-up: Design targeted substantive procedures (vouching, cut-off testing) for the areas flagged; do not treat analytical exceptions as misstatements without further evidence.

title: Confirm selected sales and balances directly with customers
description:
Objective: Obtain independent external evidence of the validity of recorded sales and receivables.

Technique: External confirmation

Steps: 1. Select customers covering material balances and a sample of period-end sales.
2. Send confirmation requests for balances and, where appropriate, specific transactions.
3. Follow up on non-responses with alternative procedures.
4. Investigate exceptions and reconciling differences.

Population: Trade receivable balances and selected period-end sales.

Sampling notes: Cover material balances; include some nil or unusual balances where fraud risk is heightened.

Expected result: Confirmations agree with recorded amounts, or differences are explained and resolved.

Exception criteria: Customer disputes the sale or balance; significant non-responses concentrated in particular customers.

Follow-up: Perform alternative procedures for non-responses (inspect subsequent cash receipts, dispatch evidence); investigate disputes; consider the implications for revenue validity.

title: Analyse revenue performance against incentive targets
description:
Objective: Identify patterns suggesting revenue may have been managed to achieve targets.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Obtain the incentive plan terms and the revenue targets for the period.
2. Compare actual revenue achievement against targets, including the margin by which targets were met.
3. Analyse monthly revenue, cut-off patterns and journal activity near target measurement dates.
4. Compare with prior periods and with cash collections.

Population: Revenue and target data for the period.

Sampling notes: Full-period analysis; focus on measurement dates and the final quarter.

Expected result: Revenue patterns are consistent with genuine business activity; target achievement is supported by cash collections and operational data.

Exception criteria: Targets met by narrow margins accompanied by unusual period-end activity; revenue growth not reflected in cash collections.

Follow-up: Direct substantive testing (journal testing, vouching, cut-off) at the areas flagged; maintain professional scepticism - unusual patterns are indicators, not proof of manipulation.

title: Inspect manual journal entries affecting revenue near period end
description:
Objective: Detect unsupported or inappropriate manual adjustments to revenue.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Extract all manual journals affecting revenue in the final weeks of the period and shortly after.
2. Inspect supporting documentation and business rationale for each material journal.
3. Verify independent approval in accordance with the entity's policy.
4. Trace entries to underlying evidence such as contracts or credit notes.

Population: Manual journals posted to revenue accounts around the period end.

Sampling notes: Census of material journals; sample smaller ones, biasing toward round sums and entries just below approval thresholds.

Expected result: Each material journal is supported, approved and consistent with underlying evidence.

Exception criteria: Unsupported or unapproved journals; vague rationale; entries timed to affect target measurement.

Follow-up: Investigate the business purpose with preparers and approvers; reverse or adjust inappropriate entries; if journals appear designed to manipulate results, treat as fraud risk indicators and extend procedures - do not conclude fraud has occurred.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Discuss incentive schemes and revenue pressures with management and those charged with governance
description:
Objective: Understand the incentives and pressures affecting revenue and assess the related fraud risk.

Technique: Inquiry

Steps: 1. Inquire of management about the design of incentive schemes and how targets are set.
2. Inquire of those charged with governance about their oversight of revenue and any concerns raised.
3. Inquire of operational staff about period-end pressures and practices.
4. Corroborate responses with documentary evidence where possible.

Population: Key management, finance staff and those charged with governance.

Sampling notes: Not applicable - judgemental selection of interviewees.

Expected result: A consistent understanding of incentives and pressures, with governance oversight evident.

Exception criteria: Evasive or inconsistent responses; reported pressures inconsistent with observed practices.

Follow-up: Inquiry alone is weak evidence: corroborate with journal testing, analytics and vouching; document the fraud risk assessment and the basis for conclusions.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Inspect large and unusual year-end transactions
description:
Objective: Understand the business rationale and accounting treatment of unusual transactions.

Technique: Inspection

Steps: 1. Identify large, non-routine or round-sum transactions recorded near the reporting date.
2. Inspect the underlying contracts, agreements and authorisations.
3. Assess whether the commercial substance supports the accounting treatment.
4. Verify the period of recording and classification.

Population: Non-routine transactions above a materiality threshold near the reporting date.

Sampling notes: Targeted selection based on size, timing and unusual characteristics.

Expected result: Each transaction has a clear business rationale supported by documentation, and is recorded in the correct period and classification.

Exception criteria: No clear business rationale; contracts inconsistent with the accounting; transactions reversed after year-end.

Follow-up: Challenge management's explanations and seek independent corroboration; consider the aggregate effect; evaluate disclosure requirements for the nature of the transactions.

title: Vouch unusual transactions to independent third-party evidence
description:
Objective: Obtain corroboration of unusual transactions beyond management's representations.

Technique: Vouching

Steps: 1. For selected unusual transactions, identify the counterparties.
2. Vouch amounts and terms to third-party evidence: bank records, counterparty correspondence, delivery evidence.
3. Where appropriate, consider direct confirmation with the counterparty.
4. Document the extent of independent corroboration obtained.

Population: Unusual transactions selected for detailed testing.

Sampling notes: All material unusual transactions; judgemental selection of others.

Expected result: Independent evidence corroborates the occurrence, terms and amounts of the transactions.

Exception criteria: No independent corroboration available; third-party evidence contradicts management's account.

Follow-up: Where corroboration cannot be obtained, evaluate whether sufficient appropriate evidence exists; consider the impact on the audit opinion; do not accept management representations as a substitute.

title: Scan revenue and journal listings for unusual items
description:
Objective: Use full-population scans to detect unusual entries for follow-up.

Technique: Analytical procedures

Steps: 1. Obtain complete revenue transaction and journal listings for the period.
2. Scan for round sums, just-below-threshold amounts, postings at unusual times, and entries by unusual users.
3. Select flagged items for detailed inspection.
4. Document the rationale for items selected and cleared.

Population: Full revenue transaction and journal populations.

Sampling notes: Full-population scan; judgemental selection of flagged items for follow-up.

Expected result: Flagged items are explained by genuine business reasons with supporting evidence.

Exception criteria: Clusters of round-sum or threshold-avoiding entries; postings outside normal hours without explanation.

Follow-up: Subject flagged items to vouching and inspection; treat persistent anomalies as fraud risk indicators for extended testing.
